# SR2e player guide

How to use the unofficial Shadowrun 2nd Edition system for Foundry VTT: what the sheets, buttons and chat cards do. For the rules themselves, use your SR2 rulebook. In Foundry, the small ? beside a heading on a sheet opens this guide at that topic. The system and this guide were built with AI (Anthropic's Claude) under human direction; see Credits and licence.

# Start here

## Getting started

This guide explains the SR2e system's screens: what to click and what happens. It does not teach the rules. For those, use your SR2 rulebook.

The system, this guide included, was built with AI (Anthropic's Claude) under human direction; see [Credits and licence](#credits-and-licence).

Open your character from the **Actors** sidebar. A character sheet has a header (picture, name, metatype), the [summary bar](#the-summary-bar), the [status strip](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn), a row of tabs, the [toolbar](#edit-mode-play-mode-and-the-toolbar) and the open tab below them. That is the *Tabs* layout; you can pick another (see [Layouts](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn)).

- **Main**: attributes, derived values, the condition monitor and skills.
- **Current**: a read-only page of where the character stands now.
- **Combat**: weapons and armor.
- **Effects**: everything acting on the character right now.
- **Magic**: tradition, spells, foci, spirits. Only for characters with Magic, spells, powers or foci.
- **Matrix**: only when the character owns a cyberdeck or a program.
- **Rigging**: only when the character can rig.
- **Gear**: cyberware, gear, drugs, diseases.
- **Upkeep**: money, lifestyle, Karma, things under way, contacts, the ledger.
- **Creation**: the creation wizard, then the creation record and the advancement log.
- **Bio**: edges and flaws, reputation, biography and notes.

A new character starts with the [creation wizard](#the-creation-wizard). A small **?** beside a heading on a sheet opens this guide at the topic for that part, and the book icon in a sheet's title bar (**Guide**) opens the whole guide. The guide window lists every topic on the left, and its search box finds words in all of them.

For a guided walk through the sheet, open Foundry's **Settings** tab, then **Tours**: *SR2e: your character sheet* and *SR2e: adding things*.

## All the tools

Every SR2e tool is in one window, **SR2e tools**. For everyone: the guide, your sheet, Defend, Resist, rolling initiative, ending your turn, the newest chat card, roll privacy, your look and settings, the tours and Report a bug. For the GM also: the GM panel and its tabs (the calculator, undo and the log, requests, setup), the NPC generator, awards, the house rules, the Skill Web, the macros and the GM panel tour. Each tool has a line on what it does, and its hotkey if it has one.

Open it with <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>, the **SR2e tools** button at the bottom of the **Actors** sidebar, the **SR2e tools** button at the top of this guide's topic list, or the toolbox in Foundry's toolbar on the left (shown while a scene is on the canvas). The toolbox group also has the most used tools as buttons of their own; its first tool selects tokens as usual.

The guide itself opens with <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd>, the book icon in the title bar of every SR2e sheet, or the small **?** beside a heading (that part's topic). [Shortcuts, hotkeys and token actions](#shortcuts-hotkeys-and-token-actions) lists every hotkey.

## Rules updated in v0.79.0

v0.79.0 corrected rules to follow the official SR2 rulebooks (the core rules and Rigger 2). The GM can put any of them back under the GM's house rules (search for the subject; the old choice is the second one).

- **Ranged combat:** recoil follows the book's table (a second semi-automatic shot +1, each burst +3, a second burst in the same phase +6, full auto +1 per round fired). You can't add more Combat Pool dice to an attack than your skill rating; resisting damage has no limit. Reloading a clip takes both Simple Actions (remove, then insert; a smartgun ejects for free); belts, revolvers and other feeds take a Complex Action. Smartlink II is −2, like Smartlink I. Flechette adds a damage level only against no armor. Thrown grenades scatter 1D6 m (aerodynamic 2D6), launched ones 3D6. Rifles, the LMG, the taser, the missile launcher, bows, crossbows, shuriken and grenades use the book's range table.
- **Surprise:** the surprise turn goes in order of surprise successes, and you can't attack someone who rolled more successes than you.
- **Seeing:** minimal light is +6 for normal eyes. Natural (metatype) low-light and thermographic vision are better than cybereyes. Glare, mist and heavy smoke are new choices, and rain and fog count as light or heavy smoke.
- **Melee:** the shorter reach takes +1 per point on its own roll; superior position (−1) is on.
- **Notice:** tick every sight row that applies (very small, partly hidden, brightly colored, very obvious, not obvious); the result reads in the book's four steps.
- **Healing:** Physical damage heals in stages, one wound level per Rest test (days, not hours); a failed first self-recovery test means you need a doctor. First aid is TN 4/6/8/10, +4 without a medkit, +2 for a magician patient.
- **Social:** Etiquette, Leadership and Negotiation roll only your side, against the target's attribute; one success gets you what you asked. Pick what you want on the book's scale, from "advantageous to them" (−2) to "disastrous to them" (+6). A suspicious NPC is +2.
- **Karma:** an active skill costs the new rating × 2, a concentration × 1.5 and a specialization × 1, whatever your attribute.
- **Magic:** your Spell Pool is your Sorcery rating (plus an active power focus); at most your Magic rating of it goes on a spell's success test, any amount on drain. Spell defense dice you use are spent until the pools refresh. An ally's spell defense can protect you when you share a player, a fight or a scene (and aren't on opposite sides), or when its mage covers you: target your tokens and press **Cover targets** next to the spell defense box.
- **Vehicles:** driving over the Speed rating is +1. Crashes and rams hurt by speed (up to 20 m/turn Light, 60 Moderate, 200 Serious, faster Destroyed). Fixed mounts and turrets halve recoil; a pintle compensates 2, the new ring mount 6. The Sensor dialog has the Rigger 2 rows (line of sight, terrain, a concealing spirit), and sensor-enhanced gunnery rolls Gunnery + half the Sensor against the target's Signature. A repair fixes all the damage in 16 hours per box ÷ successes.
- **Rigging:** dumped from a remote control deck (your drone destroyed, or your link jammed), you resist (deck rating + 4)S Stun with Body. Radio ranges follow the Rigger 2 flux table (250 m at 0, up to 25 km at 9); a deck with no signal of its own has flux 2.

## Combat rules updated in v0.92.3

v0.92.3 brought combat closer to the SR2 core rulebook. The GM can put each change back under the GM's house rules (the *v0.92.3* rows; the old choice is the second one). Under the Unified Rules Revamp nothing here changes.

- **Gunfire:** you don't dodge. **Defend** puts your Combat Pool dice into the damage resistance test (Body + pool against Power − armor). If the pool dice alone score more successes than the attacker, it is a clean miss. Otherwise the attacker's successes are set against yours: every 2 more on either side moves the damage one level up or down, and a tie does the weapon's base damage.
- **Staging:** every 2 net successes raise the damage one level, for gunfire, melee and combat spells alike.
- **Combat Pool:** it refills at the start of each of your actions. Dice left at the end of a Combat Turn last until your first action of the next one.
- **Melee:** a tie goes to the attacker (base damage). Full defense adds no dice and costs no initiative: no Combat Pool on your melee test, and your pool dice go to the resistance test, a clean miss if their successes beat the attacker's. Light, smoke and weather count half in melee (not full darkness). Subduing is +2 TN, and each further target in the same phase is +2.
- **Knockdown:** every hit that hurts calls for a Body test against half the Power (gel rounds: the Power; melee: the attacker's Strength). Beat half the wound (Light 1, Moderate 2, Serious 3) to stay put; some successes stagger you 1 m back; none, or a Deadly wound, knocks you down.
- **Grenades and rockets:** each target's resistance successes are set against the thrower's, as for gunfire. Aerodynamic grenades and launchers lose 4 m of scatter per success; rockets and missiles scatter 2D6 m (a missile also its Intelligence in metres less). Anti-personnel rockets lose 1 Power per half metre.
- **Firearms:** shotguns fire slugs unless loaded with shot, which follows the flechette rules and widens every choke metres (−1 Power and −1 TN each time). Flechette against armor uses double Impact or plain Ballistic, whichever is higher. Tracers help only full auto beyond short range. Full auto at several targets is +2 per new target, and a smartlinked smartgun wastes no rounds between them. Two rounds left fire a short burst (+2 Power, no extra level). A barrier rated above the Power stops the shot, and counts double against flechette and explosive rounds. Cylinders and internal magazines reload Quickness rounds per Complex Action. A weapon must be readied (a Simple Action) before use.
- **Attack dialog and armor:** target running (+2), target stationary (−1), attacker in melee (+2 per opponent), difficult ground and smart goggles (−1) are new rows. Heavy armor costs a Combat Pool die per point of Ballistic over your Quickness, instead of Quickness.
- **Initiative and actions:** ties go to Reaction, then natural Reaction. A wound changes your initiative at the next roll, not mid-turn. A delayed action lasts through the Combat Turn and into the next, but using pool dice while you wait loses it. Ambushers waiting on a delayed action roll the surprise test at TN 2.

## The Unified Rules Revamp (alternate rules)

The GM chooses the world's **Rules source** (Configure Settings, or the GM panel's Setup tab). **SR2E Book Rules** is the default and is not changed by any of this. **SR2E Unified Rules Revamp** is the GM's alternate ruleset: the Unified Rules Revamp follows the community document *Shadowrun Classic: Unified Rule Revamp* (v1.2), with a few house rules where it is silent. The GM's own house rules still win over it, and the house rules window marks every row it changes (search for "revamp"). A switch reaches every player at once.

Using the Unified Rules Revamp changes these:

- **Tests and Karma:** skill and attribute cards point out critical successes; the roll dialogs have a Difficulty list (knowledge skills get the knowledge table); ties on opposed perception and social tests go to whoever made the test; you can buy extra dice from your Karma Pool (one point a die). Metahumans start with a Karma Pool of 2, and each award puts its first point into the pool. Attributes cost the new rating × 1.5 (past the racial maximum, with the GM's leave, × 3), languages × 1; your native language is free at Intelligence + 2. Training takes Karma × 8 hours. Magic is capped at Essence rounded down.
- **Combat:** you don't dodge gunfire: Defend puts your Combat Pool dice into the resistance test, and if their successes beat the attacker's it is a clean miss. Damage stages on the resistance test (the attack's successes against yours, 2 either way per level). Full defense in melee adds no dice. A hit that hurts calls for a knockdown test. Initiative ties go to Reaction, then natural Reaction. Shotguns fire slugs unless loaded with shot. Strong shooters take less recoil; tracers only help full auto. Heavy armor costs Combat Pool dice; a second layer adds half. Charging is +1 Power; graded cover, running and sprinting targets and more are in the Attack dialog.
- **Health:** Stun past a full track goes onto Physical box for box. Bleeding is a box every 10 minutes, and death comes one box past Overflow. First aid lowers a wound one level (Deadly: stabilise only) and shows the treatment time; a better healer can try again. A trauma patch needs a Body test. Stun recovery is the better of Body and Willpower vs 2. A Deadly wound heals only in intensive care; a magician treated without the +2 makes a Magic loss test. Climbing, jumping, swimming and falling use Fitness; trolls run at Quickness × 2.
- **Social and perception:** the Perceive and Sneak dialogs list sound, smell, touch and taste rows; Negotiation is against Intelligence; haggling moves the price 10% per net success, and the seller rolls against your Intelligence; visible armor in a luxury setting is +2.
- **Magic:** you roll the spell's Force (plus Spell Pool) to cast. Summoning above your Charisma gives Physical drain; one nature spirit at a time. Astral initiative is 2 × Intelligence + 15 + 1D6. Ward drain is Force + successes.
- **Vehicles and rigging:** Control Pool dice on a driving test are capped at your skill, and don't go on gunnery or sensor tests (shoot with the Combat Pool), but do help your vehicle resist damage. Rigger feedback comes only from Serious (6M) or Deadly (6S) hits, resisted with Body. Small arms lose Power by Body + Armor. Passengers are hurt only when shot at, or in a crash or ram. A damaged vehicle is slower. A sensor lock is a Complex Action.
- **Drones and security:** intercepting a drone link needs a remote control deck (break the encryption first); card-reader casings are twice as hard; a passkey and a sequencer roll against the lock; a weapon detector finds everything no better than its highest die; dump shock leaves you disoriented (+2 TN) for a few turns.

Rules the Revamp describes but the system can't run (for example the alert track, an astral combat pool, team tactics) are listed for the GM in `docs/VERIFY.md`.

## Edit mode, Play mode and the toolbar

Under the tabs is a toolbar with a **Find on this sheet…** box, the layout picker ([Layouts](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn)) and, for the owner, the **Edit** / **Play** button.

- **Edit** mode: add, delete and change everything.
- **Play** mode hides the add, delete and duplicate buttons and locks the name, the metatype, base ratings and the number boxes on rows. The attribute *Mod* column, gear quantities, pools and the condition monitor still work. Click the button to switch.

Edit or Play is remembered for each character on this computer; a new sheet opens in Edit mode.

Type in the find box to hide the rows that don't match. Each tab shows how many rows it found, and folded sections open to show what matches. <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the box.

Click a heading to fold its section away, and again to open it. The sheet remembers what you folded.

Some rows have a number box: a skill's rating, a spell's Force, a gear quantity. Change it there without opening the item. The small **−** and **+** beside a number step it by one, and the scroll wheel changes the number while the box has the cursor (Configure Settings: *Sheets: − / + on numbers*). Once a character has a creation record (or, with the approval queue on, once they are out of the wizard), a player can't raise a rating this way: use [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma). Lowering still works, and the GM can type anything (see [Creation record](#creation-record-and-advancement-log)).

Row icons: the pin puts the row in the pin bar at the top of the sheet (click the row's pin again to take it off); the pencil opens the item (so does the name on most rows, but a skill's name rolls it); the copy icon duplicates it; the trash can deletes it.

You can also drag an item from the Items sidebar or a compendium onto the sheet.

**Reference** (the open book in the title bar of a character or NPC sheet) opens a pane beside the sheet that searches the Catalogue, the guide and the rules interpretations at once. Click a result to open it. Drag a Catalogue entry onto the sheet to open the shop with it ticked: you still find and buy it as usual (spells and adept powers open Learn).

## The summary bar

The summary bar sits under the header on character and NPC sheets. The monitor, pools and initiative are in the [status strip](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn) just below it.

- Grey chips list things acting on the character (statuses, sustained spells, encumbrance and so on).
- The pin bar: rows you pinned, one click to use.
- **Setup**: when something on the sheet looks wrong (an attribute at 0, ware not installed) this line lists it. Click an entry to go to it.

The quick buttons: **Attack**, **First aid**, **Rest**, **Perceive**, **Notice**, **Pay** (negotiate a job's pay; character sheets only), **Sneak**, **Athletics**, **Search** and **Social**. Others show only when they fit:

- Magic: **Cast** with spells, **Summon** with Conjuring, **Assense** and **Astral attack** when astral.
- Trouble: **Reload** with a magazine weapon, **Clear jam** for a jammed weapon, **Put out fire** while burning, **Stand up** while prone, **Break free** while someone holds you.
- Combat: **Initiative** when there is a combat; in a running combat **Full defense** and **Hold** (grab and pin the targeted token); in your action phase **Delay** (then **Act now**, and **Done** when the delayed action is over).
- Groups: **Rally** with Leadership (rally a broken group), **Morale** for a group or an NPC with a Professional Rating.
- Matrix and rigging: **Jack in** / **Jack out** with a deck, **Hitch** / **Unhitch** (ride a decker's hitcher jack), **Drive** at the controls of a vehicle, **Drone link** when there are vehicles, **Jam** with a jammer, **Bypass** when a site has locks.

Hover a button to see what it does.

## Layouts, the status strip and your turn

Each player picks how character, NPC and spirit sheets look for them: the layout picker in the sheet's toolbar, or Configure Settings: *Sheets: layout*. It changes every sheet you open, not the other players'.

- **Tabs** (the default): one tab at a time.
- **Combat column**: the tabs plus an always-open column on the right with **Defense** (Resist, Full defense in a running combat, First aid), **Weapons** (Attack, or a button per firing mode for a firearm; reload; rounds left; the hand icon draws a holstered weapon; an *Unarmed* row), **Spells** (Cast) and **Actions** (the quick buttons). In a narrow window the column moves under the strip.
- **Compact**: no tab bar; every tab is a folding section in one column, for narrow windows. Main and Combat start open. Click a section's header (or press <kbd>Enter</kbd> on it) to fold or open it; the sheet remembers. The find box still finds rows in folded sections.

The **status strip** stays at the top of the sheet with the tabs while you scroll:

- A small condition monitor (**P** Physical, **S** Stun, **OF** Overflow, in the same wound groups as the [monitor](#condition-monitor)), the wound TN modifier and the character's state.
- **Init**: Reaction + dice before the roll, the initiative this pass in a running combat.
- The pools as pips: **C** Combat, **Sp** Spell, **H** Hacking, **Ct** Control (only while jumped in), **KP** Karma; a pool shows only when the character has it. Filled pips are dice left (the number beside them is exact); click a pip to set the number (see [Dice pools](#dice-pools)).
- The readied weapon (the one you last attacked with, else a pinned one, else the first ready gun) with its mode and rounds left. Click it to attack; Shift-click to attack at once with its remembered choices.

**Your turn**: in a running combat, when it is your character's action phase, the strip says so. Unless the GM's house rule *Actions per phase* is off, it shows a pip for each action left, and buttons that need more than you have left are greyed out (hover one for why). Warn (the default) lets you click and warns you; block stops the click (the GM can always click). A projecting magician's or an unmaterialized spirit's physical actions are greyed the same way.

In Foundry's combat tracker, your own combatants show their pools, and get a shield button for full defense (out of turn it costs initiative only under the old full-defense house rule) and **Delay** in your action phase (then **Act now** and **Done**), like the sheet's quick buttons.

Other choices for yourself in Configure Settings, section *Look and layout*: *Windows: remember size and place* (SR2e's sheets and windows open where you left them; dialogs don't) and *Notifications: group bursts* (several notices at once become one, and a repeat shows ×2, ×3).

## Your look: theme, colours and text size

Each player picks the look of SR2e's own windows and chat cards for themselves (Foundry's sidebar keeps its own look). In **Configure Settings**, SR2e:

- **Look: theme**: *Street* (dark gunmetal, the default), *Corp* (a shaded light theme) or *High contrast*.
- **Look: colour preset**: the accent colour (Gunmetal cyan, Phosphor green, Magenta or Amber).
- **Look: window opacity (%)**: 50 to 100. 100 is solid and easiest to read; lower lets the map show through.
- **Look: text size (%)**: 90 to 130 inside SR2e's windows and cards.
- **Look: reduced motion**: no glows or flashes. Your computer's reduced-motion setting is always honoured too.
- **Dice colours on chat cards**: default (green and grey), colourblind-safe (blue and orange, with shapes as well as colour) or high contrast (black and white). They work with every theme and also colour the [outcomes](#chat-cards-defend-resist-and-apply).

These sit in the section *Look and layout*, with the [layout](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn) settings, except *Dice colours on chat cards*, which is under *Rolls, dice and chat*. The other sections are *Rolls, dice and chat*, *Tokens and the map*, *GM and world* and *Other*.

More choices for yourself in Configure Settings: *Floating damage numbers* (boxes of damage and healing float over tokens), *Turn pings* (a ping on the token whose turn it is), *Sound cues* (off by default: a sound on your turn, when one of your characters is attacked or hit, and on a disaster; set the volume and the sound files below it) and, with the Dice So Nice module, *Dice So Nice: SR2e colours*.

The GM can name a **Portrait folder** (for example `avatars`): a character named Rook then takes `avatars/Rook.webp` (or .png, .jpg) as its picture, as long as it still has the default picture. With **Portraits for tokens too** (on by default) it becomes the token picture as well. A picture you set by hand is kept. A portrait found by name replaces the system's [default art](#pictures-and-tokens).

## Shortcuts, hotkeys and token actions

- **Shift-click** a roll button (on a sheet, a chat card, the token HUD or the GM panel) to skip the dialog.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd>: Defend against the newest attack on a character you own that you haven't defended yet.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>: Resist the newest damage to a character you own.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd>: end your turn in combat.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd>: roll initiative for your tokens that have none yet.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>: open the sheet of your selected token (or of your character).
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>: go to the newest chat card that has a button (the keyboard focus moves to its first button).
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd>: open this guide.
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>G</kbd>: open the GM panel (GM only).
- <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>: open the [SR2e tools](#all-the-tools) window, with every tool in one place.
- Drag a row (a weapon, a spell, a skill, a critter power) onto Foundry's hotbar to make a macro that uses it.

The **SR2e Macros** compendium (Compendium Packs sidebar) has ready macros: *SR2 test…* (type a test such as `Firearms tn 5`), *Attack*, *Cast a spell*, *Perception*, *Full defense* and *Roll initiative* for your selected token, and *Defend against the newest attack*. Drag one to your hotbar. The others (the GM panel, the NPC generator, undo, a smoke cloud, exporting item templates) are for the GM.

Change the keys in Foundry's **Configure Controls** (they are listed under the system's name there).

**Using the keyboard.** Every button, link and box on the sheets, in the dialogs, on chat cards and in the GM panel can be reached with <kbd>Tab</kbd> (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> goes back) and pressed with <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>; <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> (or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>) is a Shift-click (a roll without the dialog). The control that has the focus shows a ring around it.

- A row of tabs is one stop: the arrow keys move along it and <kbd>Enter</kbd> opens a tab.
- Each condition monitor track (Physical, Stun, Overflow) and each pool in the status strip is one stop too: the arrow keys move along its boxes or pips (<kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the ends), and <kbd>Enter</kbd> fills up to that box or sets the pool there.
- A heading that folds its section: its small arrow is the fold button (<kbd>Enter</kbd> folds or unfolds it).
- A dialog puts the focus in its first field, <kbd>Enter</kbd> rolls and <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes it; the focus then goes back to the button that opened it. After a click changes the sheet, the focus stays on the same control.

Screen readers get a name for every icon button (the same text as its tooltip), the condition monitors and pools read out as, for example, *Physical: 3 of 10 boxes*, and each box says whether it is filled. With Windows' high-contrast mode on, the focus ring and filled boxes use the system's colours.

Right-click a token to open its HUD. The SR2e buttons are in the left column. On your own token: **Attack** (pick a weapon), **Cast a spell** if you know one, and **Defend** when an attack on you is waiting. On someone else's token: *you* **attacks** *them*, which targets that token and opens your attack (for your selected token, or your assigned character).

Hovering over a token you own shows its pools, monitors, initiative and state (Configure Settings: *Pools on token hover*).

With the Token Action HUD Core module (it needs socketlib), the HUD lists your SR2e actions: no extra system module is needed.

## Printing a sheet and reporting a bug

**Print a sheet.** The **Print** button (a printer) in the title bar of a character, NPC or spirit sheet opens a small window: tick *Empty condition monitor* for a sheet to fill in at the table, or *Leave out the biography and notes*. Then:

- **Print** opens your browser's print dialog. Choose a printer, or *Save as PDF* to keep a file.
- **Open as a page** shows the sheet in a new browser tab, to print or save from there. If nothing opens, allow pop-ups for your Foundry address.
- **Save as a file** downloads the sheet as a web page (`.html`): open it in any browser and print it from there. Use it when neither of the others works (some desktop-app setups).

If you own the character, a third box, *Include the notes' secret sections*, puts the secret parts of the notes on the paper too; they are left out otherwise (so a GM can print an NPC to hand out).

The printout is black on white with thin lines, so it uses little ink: the name, attributes, derived values and pools, the condition monitor (filled boxes are grey with a slash), then skills, weapons, armor, cyberware and bioware, spells, powers, foci, Matrix gear, gear, contacts, edges and flaws, and the notes. Empty lists are left out. You can print any sheet you can see.

**Report a bug.** The **Report a bug** button at the top of this guide's topic list (also in Configure Settings, under the system's settings) opens a text ready to paste into a new issue on the project's GitHub page. It holds the system and Foundry versions, your browser, your active modules, the rules source, the house rules your GM changed and the system's recent errors in this browser. Press **Copy**, paste it into the issue and describe what happened. **Nothing is sent anywhere by itself.** Read it before posting: error messages can name things in your world. (Configure Settings: *Keep recent errors for bug reports* turns the error log off in your browser.)

## Rules interpretations (†)

Where the rules as written leave something unclear, the system uses the creator's reading and marks it with a small **†**: beside a value (the narrow Spell Pool dice on the strip) or as a line at the foot of a chat card. Hover a † for a one-line summary; click it to open **Rules interpretations** at that entry.

- Each entry says what the rules leave unclear, how the system resolves it, and the sources.
- Each names the house rule that changes it; the GM can open the house rules from there.
- The whole list opens from the SR2e tools window (Rules interpretations).

They are interpretations, not rulings: the GM's call always wins.

# Rolling and chat cards

## Rolling a test

Click a name to roll it: an attribute's name in the Attributes table, a skill's name, a weapon's **Attack**, a spell's **Cast**, a power's **Use**. A dialog opens.

The dialog has your choices on the left and, on the right, the target number (TN) with a preview of every modifier that goes into it (in a narrow window the preview goes underneath). Modifiers the system found by itself (wounds, range, light, smoke and so on) each have a tick box: untick one to switch it off for this roll only. Type any other modifier in the modifier box. Where a pool can help, there is a box for pool dice. The preview follows what you change. Number boxes have − / + and take the scroll wheel.

Click the big button with the dice icon at the bottom (its label says what it does, for example **Cast**). The result goes to the chat as a card with the dice, the successes and buttons for the next step (see [Chat cards](#chat-cards-defend-resist-and-apply)).

The dialog remembers what you chose last time for the same spell, skill or summoning (Force, pool dice, the specialization box), on this computer: Configure Settings, *Roll dialogs: remember my last choices*. Weapons always remember their firing mode and options. Cancelling doesn't store anything.

Skill dialogs have a *Use specialization* box; the **Sneak** dialog has *Use the specialization* too, and the people watching count their own Perception specialization and gear by themselves.

**Shift-click** a roll button to skip the dialog and roll at once with its defaults. A spell or skill rolls without your remembered choices; a weapon uses its remembered firing mode and pool dice, but never fires twice.

How many dice you roll and what the TN should be come from the rules: see your SR2 rulebook. You choose who sees each kind of test you roll (Configure Settings: **Set roll privacy**, under *Roll privacy by kind of test*). *Foundry's chat mode* follows the mode picked under the chat box. Cards someone else must answer (Defend, Resist, a blast) are always public.

## Targets and automatic modifiers

Before you attack, cast or use a power on someone, target their token: hover over it and press <kbd>T</kbd> (Foundry's usual way). You can target more than one.

With a target picked, the dialog measures the range from your token, checks the line of sight, the light at the target, smoke between you and similar things, and puts them in the preview as modifiers. Untick any that don't fit what is really happening.

Weapons with a blast and area spells have a circle icon on their row: click it and place the area on the map. Everyone inside becomes your target.

**Take Aim** (the bullseye on a weapon row) aims at the targeted token. Each aim posts a card with the TN it gives; the next attack at that target shows it as *Aimed* in the preview.

Against a target that is invisible to you, the system rolls your test to see through it first and posts that card before the attack or spell: a Perception test against twice the caster's successes. Thermographic eyes see through plain (mana) Invisibility.

## Chat cards: Defend, Resist and Apply

Most tests post a card with buttons for what comes next. Only the owner of the character named on the button, or the GM, can use it.

- **Defend**: on an attack card, for the target. It opens the defense dialog with pool dice. Against a melee attack you pick the weapon you fight back with (with a *Counterattack to subdue* box where it applies). Once you have defended, the button is greyed for you, even after a reload; the GM gets an *Already defended* question before a second defense. A vehicle makes no dodge test (the old way, a house rule: its driver's Combat Pool or its rigger's evasive driving); a rigger jumped into it adds Control Pool dice, at most their skill, when it resists the damage.
- **Resist** (or **Resist damage**): after a hit, the damage resistance test. The condition monitor changes by itself.
- **Resist** on a spell or power card: the target's resistance test.
- **Apply (GM)**: your test changed something only the GM may change (a host, a site, a patient you don't own). The GM clicks it to make the change.
- Other buttons follow from the test, for example **Detonate** for a blast, a **Knockdown test**, **Buy** after a find test, **Use again** for a repeating power, **Rammer's damage** on the defense card after a ram. Hover a button for details.

A card that a Karma re-roll, a bought success or the GM's new TN has replaced says *Replaced* and its buttons stop working: use the newer card. A card the GM re-scored says so; the cards that already followed from the old one aren't changed.

Attack, damage and spell cards list their targets: click a name to show its token on the map. On a purchase card, the buyer can drag the item onto a sheet.

**Cards from other players.** Anyone can post a chat card with any data, so the system checks who posted it:

- Routine tests that another player's attack forces on your character (Defend, Resist, a knockdown, a toxin, catching fire, taking cover) go ahead at once when the card comes from that player's own character.
- Anything else, such as something costly or lasting (Magic loss, cyberware or deck damage, a disease, a crash), first asks you in an **A card from another player** window. It lists what will happen, read from the card's data: go ahead only if it matches what really happened.
- A card that doesn't say which character it comes from does nothing (*nothing done*).

Reading a card at a glance (colours as seen by whoever rolled):

- Solid green with **✔**: it worked (a success, a dodge, damage resisted).
- Solid red with **✖**: it didn't (a failure, a miss, a hit taken, damage taken).
- Black with **⚠**: a disaster. Purple with **⇄**: a counterattack.
- An amber outline: nothing settled yet, for example an attack waiting for the defense.
- The success count is green with successes and red at none. On a contest (haggling, sneaking, perceiving and so on) the winner's count is green, the loser's red, a tie amber, and the result line is boxed.
- The card's right edge repeats the outcome; its left edge and the strip at the top show the kind of test.

Karma buttons are explained in [Karma Pool on chat cards](#karma-pool-on-chat-cards).

When an attack or damage comes at a character you own, the system can ask you at once (Configure Settings: *When you are attacked or hit*: Open the dialog, Notify me, Do nothing). **Later (use the card)** leaves it on the card. One card asks about at most 12 targets; beyond that you get one notice to use the card's buttons. *Fold dice on chat cards* folds the dice under the summary line: click to open them.

The strip at the top of a card is coloured by the kind of test: red for combat, violet for magic, green for the Matrix, orange for rigging, gold (a sandy brown in the Corp theme) for the street, teal for health and healing. The big number is the successes; dice that hit are lit, 1s are marked. With *Dice colours on chat cards* set to colourblind-safe, blue and orange (with the symbols) take the place of green and red everywhere on the card.

## Karma Pool on chat cards

If the character has a Karma Pool, their test cards get Karma buttons:

- **Re-roll N failures (Karma X)**: rolls the failed dice again. Each re-roll of the same test costs more.
- **Avoid disaster**: on a roll where every die shows 1.
- **Buy a success**: when the test has at least one success. The label says *permanent* when the point is gone for good rather than back at the next refresh.

On an attack, use Karma before the target defends: once they have, the attack card's Karma buttons refuse.

Each re-roll or bought success makes a new card and the old one is marked *Replaced*. A re-roll carries through: a re-rolled attack gives a fresh Defend button, a re-rolled resistance test corrects the condition monitor. If the thing changed in between, it is left alone.

Contest and street cards (haggle, fence, legwork, find, sneak, perceive, social tests, negotiating pay) get these buttons for each side that has a Karma Pool, with the side's name on the button. You can use your character's side even on a card the GM rolled.

Karma Pool left shows under **Derived** on the Main tab. The circular arrow beside it refreshes the pool.

## Dice pools

The pools are the Combat Pool, Spell Pool, Hacking Pool (Matrix), Control Pool (rigging) and Karma Pool. The [status strip](#layouts-the-status-strip-and-your-turn) shows each as pips; click a pip to set how many are left (clicking the last filled pip takes one die off).

A test dialog that can take pool dice has a box for them. What you use comes off what is left. The Main tab shows the Combat Pool spent; the Matrix and Rigging tabs show theirs, with a box to correct the spent number.

An encephalon gives a small **Task Pool** for Intelligence, knowledge and Build/Repair skills: the skill dialog has a box for it (used up only in combat). An adept's Combat Sense adds to the Combat Pool, and a power focus adds its rating to the Spell Pool.

The Combat, Spell, Hacking, Control and Task Pools refill when a combat starts and at each new Combat Turn. The Combat Pool follows the book instead: it refills at the start of each of your actions, and dice left at the end of a Combat Turn last until your first action of the next. The GM can also refill them from the GM panel (Party tab: **Refresh pools**). The Karma Pool doesn't refill with them: use the circular arrow beside **Karma Pool left** on the Main tab, or the GM's **Refresh Karma Pools**. A house rule can refill Karma Pools by themselves at the start of each session or when a combat ends.

On the Current tab, **Initiative and pools** lists the initiative (and Matrix or rigged initiative) and each pool, read only. Your combatants in the combat tracker show their pools too.

## Inline tests and /sr2

A journal page, an item description or a chat message can hold a roll link, for example `@SR2Test[Firearms tn 5 mod -1]{Shoot the lock}`. It shows as a link with a die. Click it to roll for your selected token (or your character): a small dialog shows the TN, the modifier and pool dice. Shift-click skips the dialog.

In the chat, type `/sr2` (or `/sr2e`) and the same words, for example `/sr2 Firearms tn 5 mod -1`. It rolls at once (no dialog) for the speaker. A skill the character doesn't have offers to default to its attribute (+4 TN).

- What to roll: an attribute (`body`, `qui`, `wil` and so on), `perception`, a skill's name (in quotes if it could be misread, with a specialization in round brackets), or a number of dice (`6`).
- `tn 5`: the target number (4 when left out).
- `mod -1`: a TN modifier. Several add up.
- `pool 2`: pool dice (Combat Pool for attributes and skills, extra dice for a bare number of dice).
- `label Climb the fence`: the card's title. Everything after `label` is the title.

# Your character

## Attributes

The **Attributes** table has Base, Racial, Mod, Gear and Total. Type the base ratings in Base (Edit mode). *Mod* is a temporary modifier and stays editable in Play mode. Racial and Gear fill in by themselves. Untick **Add racial modifiers** in the header if your base ratings already include them.

Click an attribute's name to roll it. The plus-in-a-circle icon beside it raises it with Good Karma: hover it for the cost. See [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma).

Below the table: base Essence, natural Magic, low-light and thermographic vision, Reaction bonus and extra initiative dice, for anything the sheet can't work out from your gear, and *Drained/gained* and *Essence hole* when they apply (an Essence hole is filled first by new cyberware).

**Derived** shows Essence, Body Index, Magic, Reaction, Initiative, Combat Pool and Spell Pool (left / total) and movement. Below: Combat Pool spent, Karma Pool with its refresh icon, and Good Karma.

Anyone with Magic (adepts too) also gets the **Astral** choice (physical, perceiving, projecting). On the astral plane the row shows **Astral attack**; while projecting, **Manifest** lets you be seen and heard in the physical world (you can't act there). A projecting magician can't cross the edge of a ward region (the GM's setting). A character who can't go astral is put back to physical.

A character possessed by a spirit shows it under Derived, with **Free** to end it. A character who must feed (some infected metahumans) shows the days since their last meal; **Feed** records a meal.

The Current tab's Attributes table shows the same values read only: hover a total to see where it comes from. In the Spend Karma window, Attributes lists each raise and its cost.

## Condition monitor

Two tracks, Physical and Stun. Click a box to set the damage to that box; click the last filled box again to clear it. Each track is split into its wound groups with a divider and a label: boxes 1–2 **+1**, 3–5 **+2**, 6–9 **+3** to every target number, then box 10 (**D** on Physical: dying; **KO** on Stun: unconscious). The group the damage has reached is underlined.

**Overflow** sits beside Physical: one box per point of the character's Body (one more under the [Unified Rules Revamp](#the-unified-rules-revamp-alternate-rules)). It stays grey until the Physical track is full, then turns red and fills with damage past box 10. Filling its last box (marked ✕) means death. Spirits have no overflow. The Matrix tracks (a persona, IC) are grouped the same way, with **Crash** at the end.

The **−** and **+** beside each track take off or add one box (past box 10 on Physical, into Overflow). Hovering a box shows which boxes a click would fill or clear. With the keyboard, <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a box and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>.

The state (ok, unconscious, dying, dead) shows beside the heading. A **+N** beside Stun counts boxes past the track. You can also type the boxes in *Physical damage* and *Stun damage*.

- **Resist Damage**: for damage that came without a card. Type the damage code (for example `6M`), the armor, and tick Stun if it is Stun.
- **Hazard**: falling, fire, drowning, cold, fatigue, radiation and suffocation (heat and electric shock when the house rules use them).
- **First aid**: on this character, or on the token you target.
- **Rest and heal**: natural healing after rest.

Usually you don't touch the boxes: the **Resist** button on a damage card fills them in. A dying character shows a warning until stabilised with first aid; the system keeps track as game time passes, in or out of combat, and by default won't let them rest and heal until stabilised.

## Skills

Skills are listed by kind: active, knowledge, language and Build/Repair. A row shows the rating, any concentration and specialization, the linked attribute and the dice you'll roll. Click the name to roll it. Slotted skillsofts show under the active skills. A skill marked *martial art* (set on its sheet) is used for unarmed attacks in place of Unarmed Combat when rated at least as high.

The + on a heading opens the [skill picker](#the-skill-picker) for that kind. A kind with no skills has no heading yet: use the + on **Active skills** and change **Kind** in the picker. Row icons: raise the skill with Karma (plus-in-a-circle), raise its concentration or specialization (the square icons), pin, edit, delete.

The rating box on a row changes the rating straight away during creation. Afterwards a player raises it with [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma). The Spend Karma window's Skills list shows each skill's next step and cost.

## The skill picker

The skill picker opens from the + on a skills heading, from the Skills tab of the Add window, and from the + in Spend Karma.

- **Kind**: active, knowledge, language or Build/Repair.
- **Name**: type it, or pick from the list of common skills.
- **Linked attribute**: guessed from the name; change it if the guess is wrong. Knowledge and language skills always use Intelligence.
- **Rating**, **Specialization** and the specialization's rating (0 means the rating + 1).
- **Pay**: Free (creation, GM gift) or Learn with Good Karma. The cost shows under the form. In creation only Free is offered.

Click **Add skill**. A skill the character already has is refused: raise it instead. With training time on (the default), a skill learned with Karma starts at 0 and trains to 1. You pay for rating 1 only, whatever Rating you typed. The specialization you gave it is kept. Raise it further with [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma); see [Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time).

## The Current tab

The Current tab is a read-only page of where the character stands now. The roll buttons are on Main.

- **Attributes**: base, natural and now. Hover a total to see its sources. With a creation record, **Since** shows the change since creation.
- **Initiative and pools**.
- **Body**: armor, Physical and Stun boxes, wounds, state and metatype.
- **Karma and money**: Good Karma, Karma earned in all, Karma Pool, nuyen and lifestyle. The star opens [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma).
- **Skills**, [Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time) and [In effect](#effects-and-what-is-in-effect).

## Effects and what is in effect

The Effects tab lists everything acting on the character now, in groups: Condition, Statuses, Combat, Magic, Health, and Matrix and rigging. Rows with a time limit show the time left. The × on a status takes it off.

The Current tab's **In effect** list shows the same things. On the Gear tab, **In effect** lists drugs working now, each with a **Wear off** button. NPC and spirit sheets have the same list in a folded **Effects** section at the bottom.

**Custom tweaks** lists every tweak on your items that counts right now, with the item it comes from (see [Item sheets](#item-sheets)).

## Addictions and diseases

These show on the Gear tab when they apply.

- **Addictions**: the drug, rating and type, whether addicted (and in withdrawal), days clean, or recent doses while not yet addicted. **Kick the habit** when you can try.
- **Diseases**: progress toward recovery, a *Treated* tick box, **Resist** when a test is due and **Spread…**.

The GM can clear either with ×. A radiation dose shows as a line between them (the GM's × clears it).

## Contacts

The + adds a contact: name, level, who they are, Loyalty, what they know, a fee per legwork, their own dice for digging, favours, notes and whether they are a **fixer**. Each row shows these. Click the name to edit. The handshake **+** and **−** count favours owed either way.

In Shadowrun, **Mr. Johnson** is the name runners give whoever hires them for a job: usually a corporate go-between who never gives a real name, so every employer is "Mr. Johnson" (or "Ms. Johnson"). A contact can be one; they pay for the job and know about it, which makes their legwork easier.

**Legwork…** asks around through that contact. Say what about and pick how hard it is to find out (TN 2 for general information up to 14 for top secret). Tick it if it's the contact's specialty, or if the contact is a fixer or a Mr. Johnson (easier), or if you go through a friend of a friend (harder). A buddy or a friend for life adds dice. You can also pay extra for more dice (up to the contact's Loyalty), let the contact dig with their own dice, or **Call in a favour** for extra dice and no fee (if they owe you none, you owe them one). The card says what you learn.

**Finding things through a contact**: when you find something (*Find & buy* in the shop, **Find…** or **Buy** on an item), a character with contacts is asked how. *On your own* is the usual find. *Helped by* a contact works as legwork: a buddy or a friend for life adds dice, you can pay for more dice (up to their Loyalty) or call in a favour, a contact with dice of their own looks too (the better result counts), and their fee is paid now; a restricted or forbidden item is easier to find than openly (by default half the legality TN). A contact ticked as a **fixer** can also *find it for you*: the fixer rolls their own dice (or two per level), legality doesn't count, but the price includes their cut (by default 10%), it takes half as long again, and there is no Haggle. A favour adds dice and waives the fee or the cut. The GM sets these numbers, or turns it off, in the house rules (Time to get things).

## Bio: edges, reputation and notes

- **Edges and flaws** (when the GM's house rules use them): the + adds one with no Karma, for creation; its name changes it and the trash deletes it. The star gains an edge in play for Good Karma. The coin buys a flaw off. After creation, with the GM's approval queue on, adding, changing or deleting one by hand becomes a request to the GM (see [The approval queue](#the-approval-queue)).
- **Reputation** (when the GM's house rules use it): Street Cred, Notoriety and Public Awareness. Street Cred may be worked out from career Karma, and then can't be typed. The GM has a **Recognised?** button.
- **Biography** and **Notes**: rich text. Open the editor to write; inline tests work here too ([Inline tests](#inline-tests-and-sr2)).

Before the character has a creation record, the Bio tab also has **Create character…**, **Quick build…** and **Import a stat block…** (see [The creation wizard](#the-creation-wizard)).

## Pictures and tokens

Every new actor gets a picture and token of the system's own (unless it already has one): people a portrait by metatype and figure, with a small badge for their archetype and a rim in its colour; critters, spirits, vehicles and drones, IC, hosts, barriers, sites and safehouses a picture of their own kind. The art is the system's own, drawn by an AI (Anthropic's Claude) for it; see [Credits and licence](#credits-and-licence).

- **Picture and token** (a character's Bio tab; an NPC sheet's folded section): *Figure* picks the masculine or feminine portrait (a new character gets one from its name), and *Archetype* the badge. *Automatic* works it out: a mage or shaman from the tradition, an adept, a rigger from a control rig, a decker from a cyberdeck, a street samurai from wired or boosted reflexes or cyberweapons, a face from a high Charisma; a generated NPC keeps the generator's role. *None* shows the portrait without a badge.
- While the picture is the default art the system gave, it follows these choices (on the GM's screen, which also updates the actor's linked tokens on the map), the metatype, a vehicle's category or a spirit's kind by itself. A picture you set by hand (even one of the system's art files, or one found by name, see [Your look](#your-look-theme-colours-and-text-size)) is never replaced; **Use the default art** puts the default back on the picture, the token and linked tokens on the map (asking first).
- Only the actor's own picture and token change, and linked tokens already on the map. Tokens of unlinked NPCs placed earlier keep the picture they had.
- **Default token art** (GM panel, Setup tab): how many actors still show Foundry's stand-in, and a button to give them all the default art. The world setting *Default token art* (Configure Settings, SR2e) turns it off: new actors keep Foundry's stand-in, and the default art already given no longer follows changes.

**What the rim colour means.** The rim says what kind of thing a token is, in the same colours as the sheets' tabs and the strips on chat cards (the Street theme's shades; the other themes use lighter or darker shades of the same colours). The colours are chosen to stay apart with each kind of colour blindness, and the badge and the picture tell them apart as well:

- **Red, combat**: street samurai, mercenaries and gangers.
- **Violet, magic**: mages, shamans, physical adepts and talismongers; every spirit (an elemental shows its element in the picture) and magical barriers.
- **Green, the Matrix**: deckers, hosts and IC (white, gray and black IC differ by the picture).
- **Orange, rigging**: riggers and technicians, and every vehicle and drone.
- **Gold, the street**: faces, corporate suits and fixers, and safehouses.
- **Teal, health**: street docs.
- **Blue, security**: security guards and secured sites.
- **Steel grey**: a person without an archetype badge. **Tan grey**: a critter (an Awakened one also glows violet).

# Gear and money

## Weapons and armor

The Armory tab lists your weapons, any cyberweapons, and Unarmed. Each has an **Attack** button. Firearms also have one button per firing mode they allow.

Target first (see [Targets](#targets-and-automatic-modifiers)), then click Attack. The dialog shows the TN preview and boxes for Combat Pool dice and other modifiers. The attack card gives the target a **Defend** button, and a hit gives a **Resist** button. Shift-click Attack to skip the dialog. A weapon that may fire twice in a phase has a *Fire twice* box in the dialog (it spends two simple actions).

Row icons and buttons, where they fit: ammunition pips and reload (circular arrow), Take Aim (bullseye), place a blast area (circle), suppressive fire, *holstered* (click to draw), set up a bipod or tripod, **Repair…** for a broken weapon. A jammed weapon gets a **Clear jam** quick button in the summary bar.

Cyberweapons and Unarmed have no edit or delete icons: a cyberweapon is changed on its cyberware's sheet.

A flash grenade doesn't blind outright: everyone with a clear line to it gets a TN penalty (+6 close up, less with distance, halved by flare compensation) for a few Combat Turns; the card rolls each one's Body to shorten it.

**Armor** lists Ballistic / Impact. A piece you aren't wearing says *not worn*; open it to change that. *adds* marks a helmet or shield that adds to other armor; *parry* and *conceal* show where they apply. Damaged armor shows a minus and a repair icon. The line under the list says what counts against attacks.

The + on either heading opens the [Add window](#the-shop-the-add-window). Vehicle weapons: see [Vehicle sheets](#vehicle-sheets).

Each weapon, armor and gear row has a suitcase: click it to leave the thing behind (at the safehouse, in the car). Left behind, it weighs nothing, a search or frisk doesn't find it, and it can't be used, drawn or worn until you carry it again (armor comes off and a weapon is holstered as you leave it). The combat column lists only the weapons you carry.

## Cyberware and bioware

Cyberware and bioware, each with an *Installed* tick box. Ticking it by hand skips the surgery: use it for ware fitted before play. Ware that isn't installed has a **Surgery** button: pick who operates, the care while recovering, and whether to pay for a hospital. Recovery shows under the list with the days left; the bed icon changes the care (the GM's × ends it). Damaged ware has **Repair**; the burst or wrench icon marks it damaged or repaired. An adrenal pump has **Activate** and **Switch off**.

Lines under the list show the Body Index and other notes. Over the limit the character is in system shock (+1 TN per point over on Body tests); under the old house rule a **Rejection test** button shows instead.

A grade changes the Essence and the price. The item's Essence field keeps the standard cost; its sheet shows **At this grade** with the Essence and price the grade gives. Hover over the Essence line on the Main tab to see which ware makes up the loss.

## Gear

Everything else the character carries, with a quantity box (it works in Play mode too). Buttons appear by kind of gear: **Take** (drugs), **Apply patch**, **Play** (sim chips), **Plant…**, **Listen** and **Sweep…** (bugs), **Radio check** and **Listen in…** (radios), **Check…** (IDs), **Expose…** (toxins), **Set charge** (explosives), **Repair…** (broken gear). Chips have a *Slotted* tick box.

The cart icon looks for more of the item: a find test. Its card says how long finding it takes and has **Buy for ¥…** and **Haggle** (an opposed test against the seller that moves the price; its card has a new Buy button). With waiting on, what you buy arrives when the find time has passed ([Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time)). An item on the sheet that isn't in use (added as a wish list) leaves it until it arrives; one in use stays, and the bought copies arrive beside it. To sell an item, open it and click **Fence…** (see [Item sheets](#item-sheets)).

Lines under the list warn about unlicensed gear (with the fines), list what a licence covers, and warn about carrying too much.

On an NPC sheet, **Other gear** holds its armor, cyberware and gear as chips.

## Item sheets

Click an item's name (or its pencil) to open its sheet. The sheet shows the fields for that kind of item, in sections. The chat icon in its header posts the item to chat.

- **Template**: pick a generic or GM-saved template and click **Fill in** to copy its settings. The GM has **Save as template**, which puts the item in every [Add window](#the-shop-the-add-window), and a trash icon that deletes the picked world template.
- Weapons: the **Kind** list (firearm, melee, thrown and so on) shows only the fields for that kind. **Show every field** shows them all.
- **Cost and legality**: cost, Availability, Street Index, Legality and, where it fits, a *Permit* tick box (the GM’s: players use **Get a permit…**, see [the shop](#the-shop-the-add-window)) and a *Broken* tick box; a warning says what carrying it without a permit risks. On a character's item with a cost: **Find…** (an Availability test; its card has **Buy for ¥…** and **Haggle**), **Buy** (pay now; a player character out of creation finds it first) and **Fence…** (sell it: a Negotiation test sets the offer, and the card has a **Sell for ¥…** button). With the GM's Heat house rule on, stolen goods have a Heat that lowers what a fence pays.
- A magical site (library, circle, lodge) on a character has **Raise…** to build or raise it.
- Spells, adept powers and cyberdecks have their own sections: a spell's casting, damage, drain and sustaining (and, folded, the effects it gives while it lasts); a power's cost, level and bonuses; a deck's persona ratings, memory and options. See [Spells](#spells), [Powers](#powers) and [Matrix](#matrix).

Hover a field for what it does. The rules behind the numbers are in your SR2 rulebook.

**Custom tweaks** (every item) are for bespoke gear and modifications the rules don't cover. Press + and pick what it changes: an attribute, Reaction, initiative dice, a dice pool, a skill's dice or TN (type the skill's name), damage Power (this weapon, every melee or ranged attack, or every attack), armor, or a note only. Give it a label and an amount; untick **On** to keep it without it counting. Tweaks count while the item does: ware installed and working, armor worn, weapons and gear carried, foci bonded, powers active, programs loaded. The Effects tab lists those in force.

**Carried** (weapons, armor, gear): see [Weapons and armor](#weapons-and-armor). **From the description** (weapons): when a weapon arrives (the shop, the Catalogue, a new entry, a catalogue file, a drop) or its description is edited, the description is read for accessories: gas vents, a silencer or suppressor, a laser sight, a scope, a shock pad, a bipod or tripod, a gyro mount, a smartgun link, a quick-draw holster. Only fields still at their default are filled: a value set by hand is never changed, and "no silencer" or "sold separately" is skipped. Accessories with no field of their own (a folding stock, a sling…) become note tweaks. The line at the top says what was filled; **Undo** puts it back and stops those accessories being read again.

## Money, lifestyle and the ledger

**Nuyen** is the cash. Typing in the box writes no ledger line; **Earn / spend…** changes it and writes one.

- Pick the **Lifestyle**: its status shows the days paid or overdue, and a line under it says what it does (finding gear, resting at home, grace days when overdue). **Pay…** pays it by the month or, where the house rules allow, offers **Buy outright** (owned for good, never overdue).
- A safehouse you own has its own sheet: **Pay to build…** and **Pay upkeep…** pay from your character; the GM sets it up.
- Pick a **DocWagon** contract (when the GM's house rules use them): **Pay…** pays it by the year, and **Call** calls a team now. The biomonitor calls by itself when the wearer is dying.

The **Ledger** lists the latest 15 changes to nuyen, Good Karma and the Karma Pool, with their reasons.

## The shop (the Add window)

The **Shop** button opens it as the shop: only the tabs that sell things (weapons, armor, gear, ware, foci, programs, decks, vehicles, kits), ready to buy. It is in the SR2e tools window, the SR2e group of the left toolbar, and the title bar of your character sheet (the GM: for the selected token). The + on a heading (Weapons, Armor, Spells, Cyberware, Gear and so on) opens the same window with every tab, at that kind of item.

- Tick the **categories** above the list to show only those (Melee, Pistols, SMGs, Rifles…; Headware, Bioware…; none ticked shows everything); the list is sorted by category, then name. Search it, tick the rows you want and set the amount: quantity, rating, Force or level.
- **Pay**: *Free* (creation, GM gift, loot), *Find & buy* or *Buy now* (nuyen), or *Learn with Good Karma* (skills and spells). Out of creation a player character buys by finding: *Find & buy*. The GM, NPCs and characters in the creation wizard have *Buy now* (the GM can give everyone Buy now again in the house rules).
- **Find ticked** gives each ticked row its own find card: Etiquette (or Charisma) against its Availability TN, with the lifestyle and Street Cred; the Karma Pool works on it. The card says how long finding it took and has **Buy for ¥…** and **Haggle**. With contacts, you are first asked whether to look on your own or through one of them (see [Contacts](#contacts)). Buying pays then; with waiting on, the item arrives when that time has passed ([Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time)).
- Not found: you can try again once its base time has passed in game time. The row shows the wait (the GM can drop the wait in the house rules).
- **Add ticked** adds them (Free, Buy now, Learn). Buying or learning posts a chat line. A player's free add is whispered to the GM.
- Armor, ware, foci, programs and kits have an **Arrives…** tick box (worn, installed, bonded, loaded, ready to use). It starts ticked for *Free* and unticked for *Buy now* (a magician's focus in creation arrives bonded). Unticked, the item arrives needing that step: bought cyberware needs **Surgery** on the Gear tab. Things found and bought arrive the same way.
- Some rows keep their listed rating when bought: change it on the sheet afterwards, or add the item free.
- The **Blank** button makes an empty item and opens its sheet.
- When the GM has made starter kits, a **Kits** tab offers them: a bundle of items in one go (found line by line with Find & buy).

The list holds the system's generic templates (*Template* in the From column: plain classes such as "Heavy pistol", no rulebook data), the GM's own templates, world items and compendium items; the GM may show players less (below). A kind with no entries means the GM hasn't made any yet. The Price column counts the item's Street Index (hover it to see the index), and the Legal column shows its legality.

For the GM: Configure Settings has *Shop: what players see* (everything, only your catalogue and kits, or only what you mark) and *Shop: forbidden things on sale* (off hides Forbidden items from players). On the buying tabs you see a **Shop** column: tick your templates and world items to put them in the shop; the mark travels with catalogue files. The GM panel's Requests tab lists the **Open orders**.

The Skills tab has **Open the skill picker** (see [The skill picker](#the-skill-picker)).

**Vehicles and drones** are on their own tab: the GM’s catalogue vehicles (the *Catalogue (SR2e)* actor folder, or any vehicle the GM marks *In the shop*) and vehicle compendiums. Find and buy one as anything else; it is a new actor of your own, made by the GM’s client (so the GM must be logged in), in the *Owned vehicles* folder, and it arrives when the time to get it has passed (only the GM can cancel a vehicle order). A vehicle with no price set can’t be bought by players: the GM sets its *Cost* on the vehicle sheet (or gives it free).

**Legality**: hover the Legal column for what it means. Found openly, a *Restricted* item is harder to find (by default TN +2), and a *Forbidden* one (when the GM sells them) harder and slower (TN +4, time ×2); the find card says what carrying it without a permit risks. A *Needs a permit* or *Restricted* item can have a permit: **Get a permit…** on its item sheet (or a vehicle’s sheet) pays a share of its cost (by default 10%, at least ¥100; restricted 25%, at least ¥500) and the permit comes through after 7 days (restricted 30) of game time ([Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time)); with the approval queue on it goes to the GM first. The *Permit* box is then the GM’s to tick. The GM sets these numbers, or puts the old ways back, in the house rules (Time to get things).

## The Catalogue

The **Catalogue** is a book of everything you can get: weapons, armor, gear, ware, foci, programs, decks, spells, adept powers, vehicles and drones, each with its own page. Open it from the SR2e tools window, the SR2e group of the left toolbar, the **Catalogue** button in the shop, or the round **i** beside a row in the shop (that row’s page).

- Pick a tab, search, and tick the **categories** to show only those, as in the shop.
- Click an entry to see its page: what it is, its category and where it is from; its price, Availability, Street Index and legality; its stats; and its description.
- **Buy…** opens the shop at that entry (**Learn…** for a spell or an adept power opens the Add window).
- The GM can open the item itself and tick *In the shop* on a page.

It lists what the shop reads: the GM’s catalogue, the system’s generic templates, world items and compendiums. Players see what the GM’s shop shows them (all of it, the catalogue only, or only what is marked in the shop).

## New entries

Something the catalogue doesn't have (or there is no catalogue at all)? Make a new entry from your own book: **New entry…** in the shop (the Add window), in the SR2e tools window, or the GM panel's Setup tab.

- Pick the **Kind**: weapon, armor, gear, cyberware, bioware, spell, adept power, focus, program or cyberdeck. The form shows the fields its stat line has, each with a hint.
- **Paste the stat line** and press **Read it**: the name, numbers and codes fill the fields (damage like 9M, Availability like 4/48 hrs, ammo like 15(c), drain like (F/2)+1S, cost, Street Index and the rest in the book's column order). Check them: what was read and what wasn't is listed, and words it doesn't know are never kept.
- The line under the form shows the entry as the shop will: what it is, its price and its Availability.
- The **Description** is for your own words, not the book's text.

The GM **saves** it to the catalogue (ticked *In the shop* or not) and, opened from a sheet, can **give it** to that character. A player **sends** it to the GM: it waits in the GM panel's Requests tab, where **Review…** opens it to check and edit; saving it there approves it. Then anyone can find and buy it in the shop.

Nothing is shared outside your world. Templates and catalogue files hold what you typed from your books: keep them for your own group, and don't share or publish book text.

# Creation and advancement

## The creation wizard

On a new character, the Creation tab (and the Bio tab) has **Create character…**. It opens the wizard. The steps run along the top: Priorities, Metatype, Attributes, Magic, Skills, Resources, Contacts, Finish. **Back** and **Next** move between them; click a step to jump to it. A ✓ or ⚠ on a step shows whether its checks are met.

- Priorities: pick a letter, A to E, for each of Race, Magic, Attributes, Skills and Resources. Picking a letter another one holds swaps the two.
- Metatype: choices the Race priority doesn't allow are greyed out.
- Attributes: base ratings, with points used and allowed.
- Magic: mundane, full magician, adept or aspected, as the priority allows; tradition and totem; spells or adept powers through the Add window. A magician's foci bought in creation arrive bonded and count against the spell points.
- Skills: the + for each kind opens the skill picker (free in creation). Set ratings and specializations here; a specialization taken here lowers the skill as the trade works, and a check flags a trade that doesn't. Common skills you haven't taken are listed: click one to add it at 1.
- Resources: the lifestyle, months paid ahead or bought outright, and the **Shopping** buttons, which open the Add window. Free and bought items both come out of the Resources nuyen.
- Contacts: **Add a contact**, then its name, level (1 to 3) and role. The first ones are free; more cost nuyen.
- Finish: every build check with ✓ or ✗; click a check to go to its step. You can finish with checks unmet; the record notes it. Finishing pays the lifestyle and keeps the cash left, as the hint says.

The **Totals** panel keeps the build checks in view at every step. Closing the wizard keeps the draft: **Continue creation…** opens it again. **Finish creation** freezes the [creation record](#creation-record-and-advancement-log).

For a character made another way, **Record as it stands** freezes it as it is. **Quick build…** on the Bio tab is the older builder that reads typed lists. **Import a stat block…** on the Bio tab fills the sheet from a pasted character write-up, with a preview of what it read; the GM can record the result as the creation. The priority table's values come from your SR2 rulebook and the GM's house rules.

With the approval queue on, a character who has earned Karma can't start the wizard or be recorded by a player: the GM does it.

The wizard advises and never refuses: a metatype or magic the priorities don't pay for, an attribute above the creation maximum, or gear over the Resources budget are allowed, and the totals mark them. **Finish creation** still says what isn't met. (The GM's house rule can bring back the greyed-out choices and limits.)

## Creation record and advancement log

After Finish, the Creation tab shows the record: the build, attributes, skills, spells, adept powers, ware, gear, contacts, edges and flaws, and the folded **Build checks at the finish** (click to open).

The **Advancement log** lists every gain since: Karma in, raises, purchases and approvals, with who and when. A line above it adds them up.

Once a character has a record (or, with the approval queue on, once they are out of the wizard), a player raises ratings through [Spend Karma](#karma-and-spend-karma). Typing a higher rating, Force or level is refused; lowering is allowed. Essence can't be typed at all. With the queue on, typing more nuyen or Karma is refused too: the GM awards them. The GM can type anything.

The GM also has **Log note…** (write a line), a trash icon on each line (only the log changes) and **Reopen creation** (throws the record away and opens the wizard again; the log stays).

## Karma and Spend Karma

The Upkeep tab's **Karma** shows Good Karma (what you spend), Karma earned in all, and the Karma Pool. The GM awards Karma and nuyen.

**Spend Karma…** opens the Spend Karma window. It also opens from the star on the Current tab and from the Creation tab.

- **Attributes** and **Skills**: each row shows the rating now, the next step and the Karma. Click **Raise**. Specializations and concentrations have rows of their own. The + on Skills learns a new skill with the [skill picker](#the-skill-picker).
- **Spells** (magicians): raise a spell's Force, or + to learn a new one in the Add window.
- **More**: **Initiate…**, **Gain an edge…** and **Buy off** a flaw, where they apply.
- **Recent Karma**: the last few Karma changes, in and out.

A row you can't afford is dimmed with the reason. With the [approval queue](#the-approval-queue) on, each spend becomes a request and shows under **Waiting for the GM**. If the GM turns the queue off, cancel a waiting request with × and spend again.

Training time is on by default: the Karma goes at once and the rating rises when the training is done ([Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time)). Learning tests are on by default too: raising or learning a spell rolls a learning test first, and the Karma is paid only on success. Costs follow your SR2 rulebook and the GM's house rules.

After creation, raises normally go through Spend Karma, but ratings stay editable by hand: a raise typed in is kept, with a note that no Karma was spent. While the GM runs the [approval queue](#the-approval-queue), the lock comes back and typed raises are refused. (A house rule keeps the lock on all the time.)

## Under way: things that take time

Some things take game time. Depending on the GM's house rules: training a raised attribute or skill, learning or designing spells and other magical work, repairs, writing programs and building deck parts, vehicle work, and gear you buy: found in the shop or with a find card, it arrives when the time it took to find has passed; bought with Buy now, after its Availability time. Items with no Availability arrive at once.

While they wait they are listed under **Under way** on the Upkeep tab (and on the Current tab), with the time left and what was paid.

- **Instructor…** (training only): an instructor's test shortens the time.
- The × gives it up. What was paid comes back.
- The GM sees two more icons: the hourglass changes the time left, and fast-forward finishes it now.

Things finish when the GM moves game time on. On the GM panel, the Party tab lists everyone's things under way, and the Requests tab the open orders.

## The approval queue

The GM can turn on the approval queue in Configure Settings: *Players' purchases and Karma wait for the GM*. It is off by default. When it is on, a player who buys, adds or learns something, or spends Karma, sends a request instead. This applies to every character that isn't in the creation wizard, including one with no creation record yet. Building a character in the wizard doesn't wait.

With the queue on, a player records only spending with **Earn / spend…** (the GM records nuyen coming in), and copying an item with the copy icon becomes a free-add request, and so does adding, changing or deleting an edge or flaw by hand. Buy on a find card sends the purchase, with its price and the time it takes to arrive, and that card's Buy is then spent. Asking for the same thing twice replaces the older request.

Players see their requests under **Waiting for the GM** on the Creation tab and in Spend Karma, and can cancel one with ×.

The GM gets a notification. The GM panel's **Requests** tab, with a count, lists them: who filed it, what will run and the cost (*not enough now* when the character can't pay).

- **Approve** first shows what will really run, read from the request itself, with its cost and who filed it. A player can change a request after filing it, so check it. A name marked *(filer not verified)* wasn't seen filing it this session. If the request no longer checks out, the confirm says it won't run: decline it.
- Confirming runs it at once and pays from the character. If it fails (not enough Karma or nuyen, a failed learning test), the request closes and the player is told.
- **Decline** takes an optional reason and whispers it to the player.

For the GM: the queue is a table rule, not a lock. Every check runs in the player's browser, so a player who knows how can skip it. The Requests tab and the advancement log show what was done.

# Magic and spirits

## Magic

The Magic tab's **Magic** section is for magically active characters.

- Top row: **Tradition**; spell defense dice (held back from the Spell Pool) with **Cover targets** (target your allies' tokens first; with no targets it covers only you), or, for adepts, power points; and buttons for what the character can do: **Assense**, **Force barrier**, **Dispel**, **Signatures**, **Track**, **Enchant**, **Quest**, **Initiate**, **Ward…** (raise a ward by ritual). Only those that apply show. An ally's spell defense protects you only if they cover you, share an owner or a combat with you, or are on your side on the same scene.
- The scene environment and background count here (the GM sets them with the pencils), and a running quest with **Next stage** and × to end it. While projecting, the hours out of the body show against the limit.
- Initiate grade and metamagic tick boxes. Adepts initiate too: they see **Initiate**, their grade and only the techniques an adept can learn (centering and the others the house rules allow), but not **Quest**, **Ward…** or **Geasa**. A centering initiate fills in **Centering skill** (for example Singing); **Center** then rolls it before a magical test.
- Shamans fill in the totem: its bonuses, its environment and the dice in and away from it, *Berserk*, *Daylight TN* and which spirits its conjuring dice help. An elementalist picks an **Element**.
- **Geasa**: the + adds one; click one to change its words. Untick *Met* when a geas is broken: each broken geas adds +2 to your magical tests (by the book; the house rules can make it cost Magic instead, shown in the heading).
- **Sustaining**: spells you hold and the TN they add. The × drops one. **Quicken** or **Elemental** where allowed.
- **Anchored**: **Release**, or × to discard.
- **Foci**: tick Active; the rating is a box. **Bond** an unbonded focus for Good Karma. An addiction risk shows with an **Addiction test** button (the GM's × clears an addiction).
- **Adept powers**: tick Active and set the level. Powers over budget are marked.
- **Group**: your magical group, its strictures, and its grimoire (**Learn** a spell from it).
- **Sustaining powers** and **Under spells and powers** (on the Main tab): effects you hold on others and effects on you. The × ends one where you may.

Initiates and other magicians also get, where they apply:

- **Initiate** shows the Good Karma cost and lets you learn a metamagic technique, pick an ordeal (it lowers the cost) and initiate with your group. A deed waits for the GM: the section shows *deed pending* (the × gives it up, no Karma spent) until the GM confirms it on the card.
- **Cleanse** (lower the background count here, while perceiving or projecting), **Divine** (a question whispered to the GM) and **Invoke** (make one of your spirits a great form spirit), for initiates who know the technique. **Possess** shows while projecting; then **Leave the body** ends it.
- **Design spell** (with Sorcery) writes a new spell formula; its card has **Learn it** (Good Karma) and, in a group, **Add to** the group's grimoire. **Create ally…** makes an ally spirit by ritual (it counts for the familiar ordeal).
