Changing the **Astral** choice (on the Main tab) to perceiving or projecting during your turn in combat spends an action; coming back to physical is free. While projecting, buttons for physical actions are greyed out.

A barrier spell or a ward becomes a Barrier actor (see [Spells](#spells)). Its sheet has its kind, the current and full rating, and **Restore** (back to full). Magicians and spirits on the astral plane push through with **Force barrier**; each net success lowers the current rating.

The rules for all of these are in your SR2 rulebook (and its magic supplements).

## Conjuring and spirits

Anyone with the Conjuring skill gets a **Conjuring** section (on a character's Magic tab) with **Summon** and **Banish**, and on a character **True name…** (bind a free spirit whose true name you know). The list shows your spirits with Force, services left and kind; click a name to open its sheet. A line under it counts your bound elementals against the most you may hold.

An elemental arrives after its ritual hours (see [Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time)). A Karma re-roll of a summoning after the spirit exists changes its services (a player's goes to the GM as an Apply (GM) card), but not if its services have changed since.

A summoned spirit is a Spirit actor. A player who can't create actors gets a **Create spirit (GM)** button on the card for the GM. The spirit's sheet has:

- The top row: **Kind**, spirit type, the element (elementals) or domain (nature spirits; *outside its domain* warns when the scene's environment doesn't match), *Great form*, **Services** and **Use a service**. A nature spirit shows when it leaves (sunrise or sunset). Free spirits and allies have a **True name** (and free spirits **Spirit energy**).
- The attributes: each is the Force plus the number in the **Force +** row.
- Tick *Materialized* when physical attacks can reach it, and *Immunity to normal weapons* for its extra armor. **Manifest** shows while it is not materialized.
- Its **Attacks** (with **Astral attack** and **Force barrier**), its powers and spells (cast with its Force).
- Folded at the bottom: **Effects**, **Powers, weaknesses and notes**, and **Adjustments** (a Reaction bonus, extra initiative dice and the Combat Pool spent).
- **Dismiss** deletes the spirit and its tokens. When you may not delete them yourself, the GM's browser does it, so a GM must be logged in.

An ally's sheet has an **Ally** section: its master buys abilities for Good Karma (**Buy**), teaches it a spell (**Teach a spell…**, Good Karma per Force) and, with the sense link, uses its senses (**Master uses my senses**).

## Spells

Each spell row shows its category, type, duration, the learned Force (a box), damage and drain. **Cast** opens the cast dialog: Force, target, and the Spell Pool split between casting and drain. The drain is rolled with the cast. The target gets a **Resist** button.

The cast dialog also has, where they apply: *Anchor it instead* (it waits in the Anchored list on the Magic tab until released), *Cast as a ritual* (it takes hours; team members and an astral spotter help, and the card's **Send the spell** casts it at the end), an elemental's aid (costs a service), sustaining with a free sustaining focus, a fetish in hand, and a ward the spell crosses.

A barrier spell or a ward (**Ward…** on the Magic tab) becomes a Barrier actor; when you can't create actors the card has **Create it (GM)** or **Create ward (GM)**. Then **Draw it on the map** places its region (set the radius and click the map).

Row icons: pin, place the area on the map (area spells), cast at an object or wall (the cube, physical spells), learn at a higher Force for Good Karma (the up arrow), offer it to your group's grimoire (the book).

The + opens the [Add window](#the-shop-the-add-window) at Spells. Learning a spell with Karma rolls a learning test first (on by default) and may take time: see [Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time).

## Spell formulas and teachers

Out of character creation a magician learns a new spell only from a **spell formula** they hold, from a **teacher** who knows it, from their magical group's **grimoire**, or from a spell they **designed** themselves. The learning test (Sorcery + Magical Theory vs 2 × Force) and the Good Karma are the same in every case, but learning from a formula with no teacher is at +2 TN.

- **Buying a formula**: in the shop or the Add window, the scroll on a spell's row opens **Buy a formula…**. Pick the Force (you can learn the spell at up to it) and the tradition (hermetic or shamanic). A formula is gear: it is found, haggled, bought, sent to the GM's approval queue and delivered like anything else, and it can be given, traded or sold.
- **Learning from it**: open the formula on your sheet and press **Learn this spell…**, or use Learn in the Add window: a formula you hold is used by itself. A spell you know at a lower Force is raised; raising a Force needs a formula of the new Force.
- **A teacher**: the teacher icon by the *Spells* heading lists everyone in the world who knows a spell. The teacher rolls Instruction; their successes, up to their Sorcery, are extra dice for your learning test, rolled from the button on their card. A teacher no player plays charges a fee per point of Force.
- **The other tradition**: a shamanic formula or teacher for a hermetic magician (or the reverse) works, but the learning test's TN is higher and the study takes longer.

The GM can switch every part of this off, or change its numbers, in the house rules (Magic and critters). All the numbers are the creator's interpretation, marked VERIFY until checked against the books.

## Powers

Powers belong to critters, spirits and anyone else who has one. The row says what the power does. **Use** rolls it; the target gets a **Resist** button. An allergy has an *exposed* tick box and a **Contact** button.

The pin puts a usable power at the top of the sheet. A critter that must feed shows when it last ate, with **Feed**. On *Under spells and powers*, the GM can remove an effect you can't end yourself (dispelled, cured).

# Matrix and rigging

## Matrix

The Matrix tab shows when the character owns a cyberdeck or a program.

- **Cyberdecks**: tick *In use* on the deck you run. **Build…** builds a deck or upgrades a part (a test).
- With a deck in use: the persona ratings, **Sim** and **Connection**, Hacking Pool, Matrix initiative, Detection Factor and memory.
- **Jack in**, then **Log on** or **Operation**, **Attack**, **Perceive**, **Maneuver**, **Medic** (with the program) and **Jack out**. Once jacked in you travel with Log on; the GM has a **Move** button that goes straight to a host.
- The host lists in Jack in and Operation show only the hosts your character has found; a host's code shows once it has been analyzed.
- The **Persona** track is the Matrix condition monitor. Click a box to set it.
- **Programs**: tick *Loaded* (loading while jacked in takes time). The buttons show where they apply: **Run** for Slow and Restore, **Launch** for a frame (in a host) or an agent (jacked in), **Release** for smoke in a host. Other utilities work through Operation, Attack and the rest. **Write…** writes a new program.
- **Frames and agents** you launched: **Operation** and **Attack** (from their host), **Search hosts…** (an agent searches by itself), and the trash icon to recall one. Click a name for its sheet: what it carries, its Matrix track, **Attack** and **Restore**.
- **Downloaded data**: the files in your deck.
- A security decker of the host gets **Security**. An otaku sees their **Channels** (the + raises one for Karma) and **Complex form…** beside Write….
- On a wireless connection, type the distance to the relay to check the signal. The section also lists LTG numbers you know (× forgets one), defenses loaded, maneuvers in force and who rides your hitcher jacks (others ride along with the **Hitch** quick button).

Warnings (traced, held, crippled, a damaged deck with **Repair**, psychotropic IC effects, smoke, time on the way to a host) show in red with what you can do about them; the GM has an × or eraser to clear them.

Cards from IC and jacking out carry the follow-up buttons: **Resist dump shock**, **Deck damage**, **Resist biofeedback**, a psychotropic **Resist**, **Resist overload**. On an NPC sheet the Matrix is a section, not a tab.

## Rigging

The Rigging tab shows for a character with a control rig or a remote control deck, or at a vehicle's controls. It has the control rig rating, rigged initiative and the Control Pool (usable only while jumped in). On an NPC sheet it is a section, not a tab.

- **Take the controls…**: pick a vehicle you own (the GM gives you ownership) and drive it by hand or jump in. Anyone else is put at the wheel with **Driver…** on the vehicle sheet. The vehicles and drones you bought or were given from the shop are listed here too.
- At the controls: **Driving test**, **Jump in** or **Jump out (keep driving)**, and **Let go**. The vehicle's Handling, Speed, Body, Armor and damage show. The **Drive** quick button rolls a driving test too.
- **Remote control deck**: **Subscribe a drone…**, then **Group driving test…** and **Group attack…**. Each drone shows its Pilot, status, who controls it and its link; the × unsubscribes it.
- Jumped into a site's security system: its devices, alert and tally, and **Jump out**.

Jumping in needs a control rig, and a rigger adaptation on the vehicle (drones count as adapted; the rigger adaptation goes in on top of a remote adaptation, under Modifications on the vehicle sheet). Jumping in from outside the vehicle also needs a remote control deck, and a link that is not jammed or spoofed; out of range it warns, or stops you if the house rules say so. Without a control rig you can still drive by hand.

Damage that leaves a vehicle you are jumped into at Serious or Destroyed comes back on a card with **Resist feedback** (6M or 6S Physical, resisted with Body); a remote rigger gets **Resist dump shock** when the vehicle is destroyed or the link is cut.

The **Drone link** quick button (on characters and NPCs, when there are vehicles) intercepts a drone's remote link or spoofs it a command. Intercepting needs a remote control deck or a radio (under the [Unified Rules Revamp](#the-unified-rules-revamp-alternate-rules), a remote control deck, and an encrypted link is decrypted first). Spoofing needs a remote control deck. An intercepted link shows *Link intercepted* on the vehicle sheet until the GM clears it; with the house rule that lets a spoof take the drone over, a spoofed one shows *Link spoofed*. A character with a jammer has a **Jam** quick button.

Vehicles and drones have their own sheet: see [Vehicle sheets](#vehicle-sheets).

# NPCs and vehicles

## NPC sheets

NPCs use a compact sheet: the attributes in a grid (click a short name to roll), **PR** (Professional Rating), **Grunts** (the group size) and how many are *down*, **Threat** (Threat Rating), **Metatype** (untick *Add racial modifiers* if the ratings already include them), the summary bar and status strip, the condition monitor with **Resist Damage** and **Hazard**, and Skills, Weapons, Spells, Powers and Other gear. The NPC generator fills in PR and Threat (and a Karma Pool when the house rules give NPCs one); on a hand-made NPC you type them. The layout choice works here too.

- **Import**: paste a stat block. It overwrites the attributes and updates items with the same name. What it can't read is reported; an Essence or power cost the block leaves out is guessed, and you are told which.
- **Split** (GM): one unlinked token per standing grunt, beside this one. Morale and group attacks then count the tokens.
- A magically active NPC has the Astral choice, a **Magic** section and **Conjuring** like a character's (see [Magic](#magic)); a decker or rigger has the **Matrix** and **Rigging** sections. On an NPC these are sections, not tabs.
- Folded at the bottom: **Effects**, **Powers, weaknesses and notes**, **Critter** (Essence drained or gained, **Regenerate**, a shapeshifter's **Form** and **Shift form**) and **Adjustments** (base Essence, natural Magic, vision, Reaction and initiative bonuses, the Karma Pool and Combat Pool spent; the rotate icon beside Init refreshes the Karma Pool).

## Vehicle sheets

A vehicle or drone sheet has its ratings (Handling, Speed, Accel, Body, Armor, Signature, Autonav, Pilot, Sensor, ECM, ECCM, ECD, off-road Handling, Object resistance), damaged systems (tick tires, sensors or engine when shot out), autosofts (they help its own autopilot), seating and the Damage track (click a box to set it). **Category** and **Skill** choose the driving skill; tick *Drone* for a drone. **Design…** builds it from a chassis and a powerplant. Under **Cost and legality** the GM sets what it costs in the shop: its cost, Availability, Street Index and legality. A vehicle that needs a permit has **Get a permit…** (paid by the character who bought it, or your own).

- **Control**: who drives it (**Driver…** puts someone at the wheel, by hand or jumped in; **Autopilot** hands it back), the current speed and off-road, Handling now and crash Power. When the speed is limited, **Push…** changes it by more than the Accel. Buttons: **Driving test**, **Crash test**, **Crash**, **Repair test…** and **Reset** (GM: clears all damage).
- **Weapons**: mounted weapons; the + adds them and **Fire** shoots one (pick who fires: the driver, a gunner aboard, a security rigger or the autopilot). **Ram…** rams a target; the defense card then has **Rammer's damage**. With **Firmpoints** and **Hardpoints** set in the ratings, a line under the heading counts the points used and warns when a weapon doesn't fit. A weapon's item sheet has a *Point* choice for the mount it takes.
- **Sensors**: active or passive *Mode*, low-light and thermographic sensors, **Sensor test…** (a success locks on: the lock shows as a chip, × drops it), and **Jam…** with the vehicle's ECM. A jammed link shows in red with an × to clear it.
- **Modifications**: **Add** one, then **Install…** (a mechanic's test that takes time and charges the cost) or **Take out**. Work on a vehicle your players don't own finishes on a GM card.
- **Cargo**: the + loads gear. With *Load (kg)* or *Cargo Factor* set, the sheet counts what it carries and warns when overloaded.
- **Chase**: **Give chase…**, then the gap in metres, **Chase turn** and **End chase**. A won maneuver shows its TN bonus for the Combat Turn.
- **Aboard**: **Put someone aboard**; the × takes them off.

A drone's **Link encryption** guards its remote link against [Drone link](#rigging). Guided missiles fired at a vehicle lock on to its Signature, and sensor locks run out after a few Combat Turns without a new sensor test.

# GM: running the game

## The GM panel

Open it with <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>G</kbd>, the **GM panel** button in the Actors sidebar or the [SR2e tools](#all-the-tools) window. Tabs: Scene, Combat, Party, NPCs, World, Tools, Log, Requests, Setup. The **Undo** button sits just under them.

On sheets and chat cards, parts meant for the GM (buttons marked *(GM)* and the *GM:* row on cards) have a striped amber edge (a striped underline on small buttons). A player may see one on a sheet, but the system refuses it if they click it.

The **Scene** tab works on the scene you are viewing:

- **Scene**: background count, weather, terrain, darkness, environment tags and background count sources.
- **Regions with an SR2e environment**: draw a Region on the map, open its config and fill in *SR2e environment*: background count (aspected, toxic), environment tags, weather, light, smoke, a ward or barrier whose edge it is, or a camera or sensor that watches it. Tokens inside are affected by themselves. The list shows each region and who is inside; click a name to open its config.
- A ward's edge stops astral forms (Configure Settings, *Ward regions stop astral forms*: stop, warn or off; your own moves only warn). When someone walks into a watched region you get a whispered card with **Detection test**, or the test is rolled at once (*Camera and sensor regions*). Hidden tokens, the site's guards, and devices that are off or bypassed don't set it off; only an astral sensor sees astral forms.
- **Presets**: save this scene's conditions (the disk icon: background count and sources, tags, weather, terrain, and darkness if ticked) and put them on the scene you are viewing (the play icon); the trash can deletes one.
- [Time](#time).
- **Encounter notes**: one set per scene. Players don't see them on screen, but a player could read them from the browser console: keep real secrets in a GM-only journal.
- **Charges on a timer**: set one off now, a disarm test (select the token of whoever disarms it: Demolitions against the TN shown), or take it away with no test.
- **Fires** (start one at the selected token, spread every fire one Combat Turn, put one out, pick a fuel and mark selected drawings as fuel) and **Damaged walls** (repair fully, or a Build/Repair test).
- **Walls**: a wall's own config window has *SR2 barrier rating* (added to the target's armor when shot through it, and taken off a blast's Power; left blank, gunfire counts the default rating and a blast is stopped completely), *SR2: burns* (a fire burns through it) and *SR2: security door* (a door breaks at half its rating, a security door only at 0).

## Time

The Scene tab's **Time** shows the world time (and the Combat Turn in a fight) and buttons from **+3 s** (one Combat Turn) to **+1 year**. A week or more asks first (house rules, GM tools: the days in a month and a year, and when to ask). Moving time on is what finishes things [under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time) and runs other timers (drugs, diseases, recovery, rent, fires). [Undo](#undo-and-recent-rolls) moves the time back.

The Party tab lists everyone's things under way, each with **Change the time left** (hourglass) and **Finish it now** (fast-forward). The same icons show on the character's Upkeep tab for the GM.

What waits at all is set in the house rules, section *Time to get things*: the main switch, each area (magic, buying gear, repairs, Matrix work, vehicles), the Availability time multiplier for buying straight from the Add window, and the shortest wait. Training time for raised ratings is the *Characters* house rule about raising a skill or attribute. See [House rules](#house-rules-and-settings).

**A calendar module, or the clock moved by hand:** when world time jumps a week or more outside combat (a calendar setting the date when you turn it on, or you set the campaign's date), you are asked: **Count it as time passed** runs everything timed for it, as above; **Only the date** changes the date but not the characters' time, so drugs, recovery, upkeep and training keep the time they had left (the time of day stays the calendar's). Putting the date back the same way undoes it. The size of a big jump, or always counting, is a house rule (*GM tools*). The Scene tab's own buttons always count.

## Combat and NPCs tabs

**Combat** tab: the Combat Turn and pass, **Start**, back one turn, **Next**, **Roll NPCs** and **Add selected**. Each row has the crosshair (show and select the token), the token's initiative, ± buttons for Physical and Stun boxes, and quick icons: attack (target a token first), cast, defend, perceive, morale, roll initiative again.

**NPCs** tab: **Group roll…** (one test, one card), **Damage several…** and **Heal several…** each ask who: the selected tokens, every NPC token on the scene, or the party. **Group for morale** and **Ungroup** work on the selected tokens; each morale group is then listed with a flag (its morale test) and an × (break it up). **On this scene** lists the tokens no player owns (up to 40) with the same quick icons.

On both tabs, NPC rows show as compact stat cards (attributes, armor, initiative, weapon and damage). The card icon beside the heading switches to plain rows and back; the panel remembers.

Foundry's combat tracker gets a banner with the Combat Turn, the pass, who is acting and how many are on full defense or delaying. The acting row is highlighted, delaying combatants are listed last under *Delaying*, and full defense shows as a badge. IC, frames and agents get an act button there.

The tracker's header has **Surprise test** (every combatant rolls; hover it for how the result is used) and, when Foundry's own button isn't there, **Roll NPCs**. Rows you own have **Delay**, **Act now** or **Done**, a shield to declare full defense (out of turn it costs initiative only under the old full-defense house rule), and a line with the pools left.

## Party tab

**Party** shows a card for each player character: portrait, name (opens the sheet), player, a small monitor with − / + for Physical and Stun boxes, wound TN and state, initiative in combat (the acting one is highlighted), pools, Good Karma and nuyen, and icons to open the sheet, show the token and roll initiative again. Buttons: **Refresh pools** (the party and everyone in the running combat), **Refresh Karma Pools**, **Award Karma / nuyen** (also in the Actors sidebar) and **Heal several…**. Karma Pools can also refresh by themselves at each new session or when a combat ends (house rules, Tests and dice: *Karma Pools refresh on their own*).

**Money and Karma** shows each character's nuyen, Good Karma, Karma Pool, career Karma and lifestyle, with the party's totals, and warns when rent is due within a week. [Under way](#under-way-things-that-take-time) lists their things that take time.

## Chat cards for the GM

- Right-click a roll card and choose **Change target number…** to score it again with another base TN or other modifiers (a checklist of the modifiers that kind of test can take). Cards that already followed from it are not changed; the card says so.
- On a player's card, a TN change and any button you click that runs their test again (a Karma re-roll, **Avoid disaster**, **Buy a success**, **Use again**, **Send the spell**, **Learn it**, **Add to … grimoire**, **Detonate**, **It goes off**, **… throws it back**) runs with that player's rights. What they don't own gets an **Apply (GM)** card, as their own click would, and any other change is stopped with a *Not changed* warning. Meanwhile, anything else your browser does with GM rights waits its turn. If something waits over 15 seconds you are warned: reload the window if nothing happens.
- A damage resistance card has **Undo** (the condition monitor goes back) and **−1** / **+1** box buttons, in a *GM:* row with the striped edge.
- Defending a second time against the same attack asks first (*Already defended*); so does resisting a card again (*Already resisted*, for example after **Undo**).
- A spoofed or intercepted drone link shows on the vehicle sheet with an × to clear it. A player's intercept or takeover of a drone they don't own comes to you as an **Apply (GM)** card.
- A card with several targets has **Resist all…**: tick who resists now (no pool dice). Targets who are done, or whose player is logged in, start unticked.
- A damage card has **Apply unresisted** (full damage, no test or armor). A blast, or a shot fired through a wall, has **Barriers…** (damage the walls) instead.
- Other buttons marked *(GM)* finish what a player's test started, for example **Create it (GM)** and **Create ward (GM)** after a summoning or a ward, **Start the fire (GM)**, **Team arrives (GM)** for DocWagon, **The deed is done (GM)**, **Combine with the last blast (GM)**, **Apply to the wall (GM)** and **Add it (GM)** for a grimoire. A **Detonate** for a charge that is no longer on record (its explosive is gone, or the card is old) goes off only after you confirm its Power.

**Apply (GM) and the security model.** Players are not trusted: anyone can post a chat card that looks like a system card, with any data.

- **Apply (GM)** buttons make changes a player's test asked for. On a card you posted, or one whose author owns what changes, the click applies at once. Otherwise a confirm lists exactly what will change, read from the card's data, and names who posted it. A card whose data isn't what the system posts, or whose author owns none of the characters it comes from, is refused (*not applied*).
- **Read every confirm before saying Yes.** Go ahead only if it matches what happened at the table. Players get the same question (*A card from another player*) when another player's card would act for their character, except for ordinary tests such as Defend and Resist. You get it too when a player's card acts for one of your NPCs in a way that lasts (cyberware damage, a disease, a crash and so on).
- Configure Settings, section *Other*: *Apply players' GM-only changes by themselves* (off by default). Even when it is on, it applies only a jam, a hold, a sensor lock or boxes on something the card's author owns. The system posts Apply (GM) cards only for what the author doesn't own, so in practice almost every card still waits for your click. Each change it does make is listed in a whispered note.
- Section *Rolls, dice and chat*: *NPCs resist damage by themselves* (off by default). Your browser rolls damage and spell resistance, with no pool dice, for characters no logged-in player owns. It does this on your own cards, and on a player's card that comes from their own character. Blasts wait for you: use **Resist all…** (or **Resist** when there is one target).
- **Many targets.** One card asks Defend or Resist for at most 12 of its targets; the others' owners get one notice to use the card's buttons.
- **Keep a GM logged in.** Some of the players' actions are done by the GM's browser (without one they are told *No GM is logged in to do this*), and so are the Combat Turn and world-time timers, self-resisting NPCs and camera regions.
- **One GM, two windows.** When the same GM account is logged in twice (a second tab, the desktop app beside a browser), each of these things happens once: the window opened first runs the timers and the cards that come by themselves, and the Defend and Resist prompts open in the window you used last. Everything you click works in the window you click it in. Close or reload a window and the other takes over within a few seconds.
- **Players' chat.** A player's message keeps its colours and text styles, but anything that positions, sizes or hides parts of the screen is dropped.
- **What players can see.** Foundry sends every chat message and every actor to every player's browser; whispers, blind rolls and NPC sheets you haven't shared are hidden in the interface only. A player who opens the browser's developer console can read them. Keep real secrets (a host's codes, a plot twist) in your own notes, not in the world.
- The [approval queue](#the-approval-queue) is a table rule, not a lock: its checks run in the player's browser.

## Undo and recent rolls

The **Undo** button just under the GM panel's tabs takes back the newest step, whoever made it. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> does the same. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> takes back whichever came last: a canvas edit on the layer you are on, or your own newest logged step (a player's steps are undone from the panel).

The **Log** tab lists the steps, newest first. Each is one person's burst of changes; open it to see the lines. **to here** undoes every step down to that one. The log keeps the last 50 steps by default (house rules, GM tools); a step marked *partly* grew too big and can only be partly undone. The broom forgets the log (it changes nothing in the world). **What undo can't do** lists the limits. Changes are logged only while a GM has the world open in that browser.

**Recent rolls**: click one to show its card in the chat log.

# GM: setup and world

## Setup tab: players, tokens, kits and the catalogue

- **Starter demo**: **Create the demo** makes a small world to try the system in: four runners (a street samurai, a mage, a decker and a rigger, as full characters), a gang, a corporate host with its security sheaf, a secured building (a maglocked door, a camera, an alarm), the runners' safehouse, the rigger's car and drone, a night scene with walls, a door and lamps, and the journal *SR2e demo: try this*, whose pages walk through a fight, a spell, the Matrix, rigging and a chase, security, and printing. It is the same in every world (the generators with a fixed seed), and everything goes in folders named "Demo (SR2e)". Give the runners to your players under *Players and characters*. **Remove the demo** (it asks first) deletes everything the demo made, wherever you moved it, the combats on its scene and demo tokens you placed on other scenes. Copies you made of demo documents (duplicated or imported) stay. A player given the rigger also needs to own the demo's vehicle and drone (*Configure Ownership*).
- **Rules source**: *Play with* SR2E Book Rules or the SR2E Unified Rules Revamp (see [the Unified Rules Revamp](#the-unified-rules-revamp-alternate-rules)). It asks first, then changes the rules for everyone at once; your house rules still win.
- **Session checklist**: lines for the start and the end of a session. Tick them as you go; a button on a line does that step. + adds a line; the circular arrow starts a new session and clears the ticks.
- **Players and characters**: pick the character each player plays, then **Save who plays whom**. The player becomes its owner. **Award to several…** gives Karma and nuyen.
- **Token setup**: linked tokens, Physical and Stun bars, vision from eyes and cyberware, who sees names and bars, disposition, and whether tokens already on scenes change too (*Relink unlinked ones* drops those tokens' own changes). Apply it to **The party's tokens** or **Pick actors…**.
- **Portraits by name**: with a *Portrait folder* set in Configure Settings (see [Your look](#your-look-theme-colours-and-text-size)), **Find portraits for every actor** gives each actor that still has the default picture the one named after it.
- **Starter kits**: bundles of items. Make one from a sheet (+) or empty (the box), drop items on it, edit it (pencil), and give it to actors (the gift): it asks whether things arrive ready to use (installed, worn, bonded). Players find kits on the Add window's Kits tab.
- **Item catalogue**: the world's item templates, which show first in every [Add window](#the-shop-the-add-window). **Paste spreadsheet rows…**, **Export as CSV**, **Manage templates…**, save or load a catalogue file, and templates to or from a compendium. A catalogue file holds templates and kits (to take to another world) and can also hold vehicles and drones, NPCs, critters and spirits, so one file can bring a whole data set into a world. **Load a catalogue file…** shows what the file has and asks first. New actors go in the folder *Catalogue (SR2e)*, sorted into subfolders (vehicles and drones by kind, spirits, critters, NPCs; actors left at the top of the folder by an earlier load are sorted too, and anything you moved elsewhere stays put); an actor already in the world with the same name is never replaced. With *Fill in missing values* ticked, items already in the world with the same type and name (on characters too, and on actors the file also has) get the file's descriptive values (cost, Availability, a damage code, ranges, Essence…) only where theirs are still empty or zero. A value someone set is kept, and ratings, quantities, ammo, accessories and on/off switches are never changed. An actor already in the world is never changed itself. Any item sheet also has **Save as template**.
- **Characters from a stat block**: paste a character write-up to make a new character.
- **Modules**: which helpful modules are on, a tour of the GM panel, and a link to this guide.

## Scene builder

The **Scene builder** walks you through making a scene with everything in one place, then builds it in one go. Open it from the **SR2e tools** window (<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>), the toolbar's toolbox, the button in the Scenes sidebar, or **New scene…** at the top of the GM panel's Scene tab. Every step can be skipped, the column on the right shows what you have so far, and nothing is made until you press **Build the scene**.

- **Basics**: the name, the folder, what kind of place it is (*Real world*, *Astral* or *Matrix host*), and its size in metres with the grid. The kind picks sensible defaults: an astral or Matrix scene is lit everywhere and gets its own backdrop, and a Matrix scene gets a host. Characters still project, perceive or jack in themselves, as on any scene.
- **Map**: one of the backdrops drawn for the system (streets, an alley, a rooftop, a warehouse, an office floor, a club, sewers, a garage, docks, a forest, the astral plane, a host, the grid), a plain colour, or a picture of your own. A built-in backdrop brings its size and, ticked, walls, doors and lamps that match the picture. Token vision and fog of war are set here too.
- **Time and conditions**: the time of day sets the darkness (day, dusk and dawn, night, darker in the wilds; indoors the lamps light it), or type your own darkness. The light level it gives is shown. You can also move world time to that hour (it asks first: every timer runs). Weather and the vehicle terrain are the Scene tab's settings.
- **Magic**: background count and its sources, environment tags for totems, and a ward or barrier over the whole scene or the NPCs' area (a barrier actor and a region on the map).
- **Who's there**: tick the player characters, then add NPCs, spirits and critters from your actors (the list, or drag them in from the Actors sidebar) or made by the NPC generator (a person, a group, a spirit, critters, each with a Threat Level; roll again to change them). Each row sets how many, whether they are hidden, their attitude (the token's disposition) and whether they are one morale group. Player characters start in one area of the map and everyone else in another. Copies of an actor are unlinked tokens; tick *Unique* for a named NPC whose sheet is the token's.
- **Security and Matrix**: a host and a security site, either ones you have or made for the scene. A new site puts a maglock on the backdrop's secure doors, with cameras and an alarm rated by Threat; its host is the one above. On a Matrix scene the host's token stands on the map, and its IC arrives from its security sheaf as the tally climbs.
- **Finish**: your notes, a GM journal entry (the notes, the summary and links to everything made), music, the combat tracker (everyone added to a new combat, and the NPCs' initiative rolled if you like), and whether to view the scene yourself or show it to the players.

Opened on an existing scene (**Change this scene…** in the Scene tab, or *Change with the Scene builder* in a scene's menu in the sidebar), it starts from that scene's settings. What you change there is changed, and the people, ward, site and host you pick are added; nothing already on the scene is deleted, its size stays, and a backdrop's walls are only added to a scene with no walls yet.

**Save as a template** (on the Finish step) keeps every choice, including who's there, so the same kind of scene takes one click next time: load it on the Basics step. Everything the builder makes is marked, so **Remove this scene and what the builder made** (it asks first) deletes the scene, the actors and journal it made for it and the combats on it, and leaves your own actors and journals alone.

## World tab, hosts, sites and safehouses

The **World** tab lists **Magical groups** (new, edit, a broken stricture, the grimoire), Matrix hosts (tally, alert to pick, reset, clear smoke), **Building security** sites (tally, alert to pick) and **Safehouses** with upkeep.

- A **host** sheet has its node kind, the grid it is on and an LTG number to dial, the security code and value, the subsystems, the tally and alert (**Reset tally**; each intruder's own tally is listed), a shutdown in progress (**Dump now**) and the valid passcodes (× takes one away). It holds the **Security sheaf** (**Generate sheaf** rolls one for the host's code and value, replacing the steps; hosts the NPC generator makes come with one), **IC** (**Launch IC**), **Data stores** (**Add file**, **Generate paydata**, **Reset found**), the deckers inside, security deckers, subsystem data bombs and, on an LTG, comcalls.
- An **IC** sheet sets its type, category, rating, damage, behavior (what it guards, what a trace does, a psychotropic payload), a *Party* name (IC with the same party act together: **Party attack**), construct behaviors and its host. Buttons: **Attack** (or **Act**), **Locate** (find a decker who broke contact) and **Restore**.
- A **site** sheet has its alert, security tally (with the next step and **Reset**) and who responds, and how many Combat Turns or minutes after an alert they arrive. **Devices**: **Add device**, then per row link the selected token (where a camera sees from) or door wall (what a lock holds), switch it on or off, mark it bypassed, smash it, and **Scan…**, **Detect…** or **Bypass…**. **Guards**: select their tokens and press +, then **Guards look…**. Also **Security steps** (**Add step**), the **Security rigger** (**Security rigger…**, **Jump out**), **Turrets and drones** (vehicle actors with a mounted weapon; a **Fire** button per weapon) and a linked Matrix host: the site and the host raise each other's alerts, and a lockdown locks every linked door that isn't bypassed.
- A **safehouse** sheet totals its cost, upkeep, space, comfort, security and the rest. **Pay to build…** and **Pay upkeep…** pay from a character you own; it can make the matching security site, ward and home host actors, and give a magician its library or lodge. **People** lists owners and residents, and **Build it** adds options by category. The GM also has **Search for it…** (someone looking for it) and the amount paid towards building, under the notes.

Hover a button for what it does. The rules behind them are in your SR2 rulebook and its supplements.

## Tools tab: NPC generator and calculator

- **Open the NPC generator** (also a button in the Actors sidebar): choose what to generate (a person, a group, an organisation, a contact, a spirit, a critter, a fixer's job, street names), a Threat Level from 0 to 5 and the options for that kind. People can arrive as tokens on the viewed scene, hidden from the players, and a group can be grouped for morale.
- The **Preview** shows the result first; the line beside the buttons says what **Create** will do. **Re-roll** rolls again, and **Post to GM** whispers the preview. **Create** makes the actors in a *Generated (SR2e)* folder; an organisation or a job becomes a GM journal entry (plus its people if ticked), street names are posted to the GMs, and a contact can go straight onto a character's Contacts.
- **Dice and TN calculator**: dice, base TN and modifiers (one per line, like `Smoke +4`) give the TN, each die's chance, the successes to expect, the chance of a disaster and of at least 1, 2, 3… successes. **Roll it** posts a card with your label, to the players too if you tick that.

## House rules and settings

Configure Settings, SR2e system: **Edit house rules** opens a window of rule values for this world, in sections: Tests and dice, Characters, Ranged combat, Gear, Magic and the Matrix, Street, Magic and critters, Initiative and actions, Melee, Vehicles and rigging, Building security, Upkeep, Tokens, GM tools, NPC generator, *Time to get things* (see [Time](#time)), Safehouses and six *Unified Rules Revamp* sections, then *Advanced* (any other rule by its path, as JSON). **Save** applies the changes for everyone at once, and open sheets redraw by themselves.

Under each row are its default and *changed* when your value differs. With the Revamp as the rules source, the default shown is the Revamp's, and the rows it changes are marked with the book's value. A row above wins over the same path under Advanced. If the Advanced box isn't valid JSON, nothing is saved and the window stays open. **Reset all to defaults** clears your house rules for both rules sources. A house rule the system can't use (an unknown rule, or the wrong kind of value) is left out, and the GM gets a whispered list when the world loads.

The **Find a rule…** box at the top shows only the rows that match (and opens their sections); the links under it jump to a section. Click a section's title to fold it.

The rules changes made since v0.70.0 (dying out of combat, fresh pools at the start of a combat, holds, Take Aim, firing twice, Karma on contest cards, owned lifestyles, drone links, firmpoints and hardpoints, missiles, NPC ratings and many more) each have a switch here, a row or a value under Advanced, that puts the old way back. Search for the subject; many rows name the old choice *(old)*.

Configure Settings itself is in sections:

- *GM and world*: **Edit house rules**, **Edit the Skill Web** (defaulting links between skills), *Players' purchases and Karma wait for the GM* ([the approval queue](#the-approval-queue), off by default) and *Support for Item Piles and Health Estimate* (on; it needs a reload) and *One look for module windows* (on: with Foundry's dark colour scheme, each user's Monk's Enhanced Journal gets its own dark backgrounds once, where they are still at Monk's default).
- *Tokens and the map*: *Ward regions stop astral forms* and *Camera and sensor regions* (see [The GM panel](#the-gm-panel)), and each player's own *Floating damage numbers*, *Turn pings* and *Pools on token hover*.
- *Rolls, dice and chat*: *NPCs resist damage by themselves* (see [Chat cards for the GM](#chat-cards-for-the-gm)), and each player's own roll privacy, dice colours and sound cues (off by default, with a volume and a sound file for each cue; the security alert cue is the GM's).
- *Other*: *Rules source* (see [the Unified Rules Revamp](#the-unified-rules-revamp-alternate-rules)), *Apply players' GM-only changes by themselves* and each player's *Dice So Nice: SR2e colours*.
- *Look and layout*: each player's own look (see [Your look](#your-look-theme-colours-and-text-size)).

Many values were entered from memory and need checking against your SR2 rulebook: the list is `docs/VERIFY.md` in the project's source.
